DAMGHANI:v1p110/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p110/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p110/r11.claim: The verb janna means to cover or conceal.
DAMGHANI:v1p110/r11.anchor: السابع جن أي ستر قوله تعالى في سورة الأنعام فلما جن عليه الليل

NAHHAS:v2p76/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p76/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p76/r3.claim: قال هذا ربي is a subject-predicate clause.
NAHHAS:v2p76/r3.anchor: مفعول ( قال هذا ربي ) ابتداء وخبر

NAHHAS:v2p76/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p76/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v2p76/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the believer knows God in the heart and through signs; when God makes Himself known, knowledge becomes light upon light, as with Abraham.
NAHHAS:v2p76/r4.anchor: ما صح عن ابن عباس رحمه الله أنه قال في قول الله

NAHHAS:v2p76/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p76/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p76/r5.claim: Abraham first knew his Lord through his heart and signs, then gained greater knowledge when God revealed Himself, saying أتحاجوني في الله وقد هدان.
NAHHAS:v2p76/r5.anchor: إبراهيم صلى الله عليه وسلم عرف الله عز وجل بقلبه واستدل عليه بدلائله

MUQATIL:6:76-80/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:76-80/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:76-80/r1.claim: At the end of the month Abraham sees Venus from a cave; its setting, then the setting of the larger, brighter moon and sun, proves that none is his enduring Lord, and he seeks guidance lest he stray.
MUQATIL:6:76-80/r1.anchor: دنا من باب السرب، وذلك فى آخر الشهر، فرأى الزهرة أول الليل من خلال السرب

TABATABAI:6:74-83#13/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#13/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#13/r1.claim: The demonstrative thus links the vision of the heavenly kingdom to Abraham’s preceding recognition that idol worship is error; the following night scene continues the account. The present-form verb narrates a past event.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#13/r1.anchor: فالمعنى أنا أرينا إبراهيم ملكوت السماوات والأرض فبعثه ذلك أن حاج أباه وقومه في أمر الأصنام

TABATABAI:6:74-83#16/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#16/r1.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:6:74-83#16/r1.claim: Al-Rāghib says the root j-n-n concerns hiding something from the senses; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī explains that night covering Abraham means darkness settling, not merely sunset.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#16/r1.anchor: أصل الجن بفتح الجيم ستر الشيء عن الحاسة يقال جنه الليل وأجنه وجن عليه

TABATABAI:6:74-83#16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#16/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#16/r2.claim: The night-and-star scene follows from Abraham’s rejection of idols and his prior vision of the kingdom: after God showed him creation’s dependence, night came and he saw a star.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#16/r2.anchor: نريه الملكوت من الأشياء فأبطل ألوهية الأصنام

TABATABAI:6:74-83#16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#16/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#16/r3.claim: The indefinite a star avoids identifying a particular celestial body because Abraham’s argument applies to any setting star; the wording does not support an arbitrary pointed star among countless stars.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#16/r3.anchor: فلا غرض في الكلام يتعلق بتعيين هذا الكوكب وأنه أي كوكب كان من السيارات أو الثوابت

TABATABAI:6:74-83#17/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#17/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#17/r4.claim: Here rabb means the owner or manager who governs affairs, not the Creator of heaven and earth, who is incorporeal, uncontained by place, and not an object of pointing.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#17/r4.anchor: مالك الأشياء المربوبين، المدبر لأمرهم لا الذي فطر السماوات والأرض

TABATABAI:6:74-83#17/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#17/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#17/r5.claim: Abraham already knew God; polytheists and Sabians generally assigned created subordinate beings delegated control over particular domains, so this is my lord identifies a proposed governor, not a creator equal to God.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#17/r5.anchor: أراد به إثبات أنه رب يدبر الأمر لا إله فاطر مبدع

TABATABAI:6:74-83#19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#19/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#19/r3.claim: Afūl means setting; a setting star cannot govern continuously, while real lordship entails a lasting relation that draws the dependent creature to love its Lord.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#19/r3.anchor: وفيه إبطال ربوبية الكوكب بعروض صفة الأفول له فإن الكوكب الغارب ينقطع بغروبه ممن طلع عليه

TABATABAI:6:74-83#19/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#19/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#19/r4.claim: A true Lord must be permanent and unchanging; people attach themselves to transient beauty only when desire distracts them from its passing away.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#19/r4.anchor: فمن الواجب أن يكون الرب ثابت الوجود غير متغير الأحوال كهذه الزخارف المزوقة

TABATABAI:6:74-83#19/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#19/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#19/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī insists that the setting-star reasoning is a demonstrative argument, even if it might look like rhetoric or poetry.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#19/r5.anchor: وهذا وجه برهاني وإن كان ربما يتخيل أنه بيان خطابي أو شعري

TABATABAI:6:74-83#19/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#19/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#19/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī cites a report from al-Ṣādiq asking whether religion is anything but love, in support of the connection between worship and love.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#19/r6.anchor: وقد ورد في المروي عن الصادق عليه السلام

TABATABAI:6:74-83#20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#20/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#20/r1.claim: The direct proof is that lordship entails being loved, while what lacks enduring beauty cannot command natural love and therefore cannot be Lord.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#20/r1.anchor: لأن الربوبية والألوهية تلازمان المحبوبية فما لا يتعلق به الحب الغريزي الفطري

TABATABAI:6:74-83#20/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#20/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#20/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī prefers the direct argument: lordship entails being loved, while what lacks enduring beauty cannot command natural love and therefore cannot be Lord.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#20/r2.anchor: وهذا الوجه هو الظاهر يتكئ عليه سياق الاحتجاج في الآية

TABATABAI:6:74-83#20/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#20/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#20/r4.claim: By using the language of rational beings for what he does not love, Abraham suggests that objects without awareness or reason cannot merit lordship, as in his questions about idols’ hearing, benefit, and harm.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#20/r4.anchor: وكأنه للإشارة إلى أن غير أولي الشعور والعقل لا يستحق الربوبية من رأس

TABATABAI:6:74-83#21/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#21/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#21/r5.claim: The sequence suggests Abraham stayed with the star hypothesis until he saw it set; had he known it would set, he could have refuted its lordship as directly as he refuted idols.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#21/r5.anchor: فإن فيه إشعارا بأنه عليه السلام مكث بانيا على كون الكوكب ربا حتى شاهد غروبه

TABATABAI:6:74-83#24/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#24/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:6:74-83#24/r2.claim: Some commentators reduce I do not love those that set to a popular insinuation that the ignorant worshippers’ stars become hidden from them and do not know their worshippers’ affairs.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#24/r2.anchor: إذ يقول والصواب أن الكلام كان تعريضا خفيا لا برهانا نظريا جليا

TABATABAI:6:74-83#24/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#24/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#24/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects the popular-argument reading: the surrounding certainty and malakūt passages show the proof is demonstrative, and it rests on love and its absence, not on setting alone.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#24/r3.anchor: وخفي عليه ثانيا أن الحجة بنيت على الحب وعدمه لا على الأفول

TABATABAI:6:74-83#25/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#25/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#25/r3.claim: I do not love those that set means beings who disappear and do not endure cannot command human love; since the worshipped Lord must be loved, setting celestial bodies cannot be lords.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#25/r3.anchor: أن الذي من شأنه أن يفقده الإنسان ويغيب عنه ولا يبقى ولا يثبت له لا يستحق أن يحبه الإنسان

TABATABAI:6:74-83#25/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#25/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#25/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the opposing commentator confuses rising with a trait of lordship; the verse does not build its proof on rising, so that reading leaves the question unanswered.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#25/r4.anchor: هو البزوغ وهو الطلوع والظهور بعد خفاء المنافي للربوبية

TABATABAI:6:74-83#25/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#25/r5.speaker: الكشاف
TABATABAI:6:74-83#25/r5.claim: Al-Kashshāf says setting makes the argument clearer than rising because it involves concealment; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī answers that only setting frustrates the love required by lordship, whereas rising does not.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#25/r5.anchor: الاحتجاج بالأفول أظهر لأنه انتقال مع خفاء واحتجاب

TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r1.claim: Abraham's proof turns on refusing love for anything liable to set, not on setting alone; therefore it does not depend on a special contrast with rising.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r1.anchor: إنما هو بعدم تعلق الحب لا بالأفول حتى يوجه العدول إليه من البزوغ

TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r2.claim: The dispute concerns whether celestial beings govern the earthly or human realm, not whether they are the ultimate source of all existence and governance.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r2.anchor: نفي ربوبية الأجرام الثلاثة بمعنى تدبيرها للعالم الأرضي أو العالم الإنساني

TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r3.claim: Some commentators make setting proof of contingency, which entails dependence on a necessary existent; Tabatabai says this misses the pagans' actual position.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r3.anchor: قول بعضهم إن الأفول إنما أخذ مبدءا للبرهان لأنه يستلزم الإمكان

TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r4.speaker: آخرون
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r4.claim: Others infer from setting as motion that a mover must ultimately be unmoved; Tabatabai says this proof targets deniers of a creator, not star worshippers.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r4.anchor: ما في قول آخرين إن الأفول إنما ينفي الربوبية عن المتصف به لأنه حركة

TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r5.claim: Sabians and star worshippers already regard celestial bodies as dependent on God, so contingency and motion arguments do not answer their claim to subordinate governance.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r5.anchor: وعبدة الكواكب من الصابئين وغيرهم وإن ذهبوا إلى أن كل جرم سماوي قديم زماني

TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r6.claim: The objection that setting means contingency or motion misrepresents its proponents: they infer those consequences from setting rather than defining the word that way.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r6.anchor: هؤلاء لا يقولون إن الأفول في الآية بمعنى الإمكان أو بمعنى الحركة

TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r7.claim: Mere disappearance cannot disprove lordship: God is unseen without changing, and celestial disappearance is due to Earth's daily motion and our changed viewpoint.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#26/r7.anchor: الواجب تعالى أيضا غائب عن مشاعرنا من غير أن يتحول عليه الحال

TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r1.speaker: الرازي
TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r1.claim: Al-Razi says setting and rising both indicate origination, but setting is clearer to ordinary people because a star loses its apparent power then.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r1.anchor: وقد أراد الرازي أن يجمع بين الوجوه جميعا فقال في تفسيره ما نصه

TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r2.speaker: الرازي
TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r2.claim: Al-Razi distinguishes audiences: motion's proof of origination is certain but subtle, while setting's visible loss of dominion is evident to everyone.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r2.anchor: أما دلالة الأفول فإنها دلالة ظاهرة يعرفها كل أحد

TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r3.speaker: بعض المحققين
TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r3.claim: For the spiritually discerning, setting signifies contingency: every possible thing remains dependent until the chain ends at the one beyond possibility.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r3.anchor: قال بعض المحققين الهوي في خطرة الإمكان افول

TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r4.speaker: الرازي
TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r4.claim: For an intermediate audience, setting signifies motion; every moving thing is originated and depends on the eternal, powerful Creator.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r4.anchor: وأما الأوساط فإنهم يفهمون من الأفول مطلق الحركة

TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r5.speaker: الرازي
TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r5.claim: For ordinary viewers, a setting star loses light, power, and authority, so it cannot be divine; one phrase addresses all three levels of understanding.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r5.anchor: وأما العوام فإنهم يفهمون من الأفول الغروب

TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r6.speaker: الرازي
TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r6.claim: Al-Razi adds that astrologers considered planets weak near western setting, making setting especially damaging to their claim of celestial divinity.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#27/r6.anchor: ومذهب أصحاب النجوم أن الكوكب إذا كان في الربع الشرقي

TABATABAI:6:74-83#28/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#28/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#28/r1.claim: Al-Razi's audience-based layers are neither indicated by the verse nor effective against star worshippers, who already treat celestial bodies as dependent beings governing what lies below.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#28/r1.anchor: ما تفنن به من تقسيم البرهان إلى حصص مختلفة باختلاف النفوس

TABATABAI:6:74-83#28/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#28/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#28/r2.claim: Motion proves that a thing is originated with respect to its moving description, not that its underlying substance began to exist; the full proof belongs elsewhere.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#28/r2.anchor: الحركة إنما تدل على حدوث المتحرك من حيث وصفه وهو التحرك لا من حيث ذاته

TABATABAI:6:74-83#28/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#28/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#28/r3.claim: Abraham argued from what God showed him in the heavens and from visible phenomena as the conversation allowed, either because he had not seen every daily event or to use evidence his people could observe.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#28/r3.anchor: ساق هذه الحجج بحسب ما كان الله سبحانه يريه ملكوت السماوات والأرض

TABATABAI:6:74-83#28/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#28/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#28/r4.claim: The omission of the sun may mean the daytime debate with his family and people left no time before night; clouds or the people's presence only at sunrise are other possibilities.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#28/r4.anchor: من المحتمل أن يكون قد خرج إلى قومه للمحاجة والوقت لا يسع أزيد

TABATABAI:6:74-83#31/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#31/r4.speaker: محمد بن مسلم
TABATABAI:6:74-83#31/r4.claim: One of the two Imams says Abraham was seeking his Lord when he saw a star and had not reached disbelief; anyone who reflects in that way is like him.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#31/r4.anchor: عن محمد بن مسلم عن أحدهما عليهما السلام قال في إبراهيم إذ رأى كوكبا

TABATABAI:6:74-83#31/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#31/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:6:74-83#31/r5.claim: Al-Qummi reports al-Sadiq's view that Abraham did not commit shirk by saying “this is my Lord”; he was seeking his Lord, whereas such a statement by another person is shirk.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#31/r5.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي قال وسئل أبو عبد الله عليه السلام عن قول إبراهيم

TABATABAI:6:74-83#31/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#31/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#31/r6.claim: Tabatabai distinguishes Abraham, still seeking before conclusive explanation, from anyone who is no longer a seeker after clear proof has been established.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#31/r6.anchor: الذي هو طالب من تم له البيان وقامت له الحجة الواضحة فهو غير طالب

TABATABAI:6:74-83#31/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#31/r7.speaker: حجر
TABATABAI:6:74-83#31/r7.claim: Al-Ayyashi transmits Hajar's question to al-Sadiq about Abraham's words; the Imam repeats that Abraham sought his Lord, while the same words from another are shirk.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#31/r7.anchor: عن حجر قال أرسل العلاء بن سيابة يسأل أبا عبد الله عليه السلام

TABATABAI:6:74-83#31/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#31/r8.speaker: محمد بن حمران
TABATABAI:6:74-83#31/r8.claim: Asked about Abraham's words, al-Sadiq says they did not amount to anything and that Abraham intended something other than the apparent wording.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#31/r8.anchor: وفيه عن محمد بن حمران قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام

TABATABAI:6:74-83#32/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#32/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#32/r1.claim: Tabatabai explains that “this is my Lord” carries no assertion beyond its wording: Abraham used a hypothetical concession or assumed premise to expose its false consequence.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#32/r1.anchor: لا يتعدى مفهوم نفسه وليس له وراء ذلك معنى يحكي عنه

TABATABAI:6:74-83#55/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#55/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#55/r2.claim: The objection that Abraham could only have debated celestial worshippers after reaching Harran is, the author concludes, a problem for his earlier interpretation of the passage rather than for the Qur'an itself.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#55/r2.anchor: وهذا في الحقيقة إشكال على التفسير الذي تقدم إيراده في بيان الآيات لا على أصل الكتاب

THALABI:v4p162#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p162#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p162#2/r7.claim: The account says Ibrahim first saw Jupiter, or Venus, before the moon late in the month and called the star his lord.
THALABI:v4p162#2/r7.anchor: وإنما سميت الجن لاجتنانها فلا ترى

THALABI:v4p162#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p162#2/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p162#2/r8.claim: جن عليه الليل means night fell and became dark; related forms mean to cover or grow dark, and jinn are named for being hidden from sight.
THALABI:v4p162#2/r8.anchor: فذلك قوله عز وجل: فلما جن عليه الليل أي دخل يقال: جن الليل وأجن وجنه الليل

THALABI:v4p163/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p163/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
THALABI:v4p163/r1.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses جنون الليل as its darkness and cites a line about night sheltering a ride; no poet is named in the passage.
THALABI:v4p163/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: جنون الليل سواده، وأنشد: فلولا جنان الليل أدرك ركضنا

THALABI:v4p163/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p163/r2.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v4p163/r2.claim: One view takes Ibrahim’s statements at face value: he was a child before proof and guidance, when he was neither an unbeliever nor a believer.
THALABI:v4p163/r2.anchor: فأجراه بعضهم على الظاهر. وقالوا: ما كان إبراهيم (عليه السلام) مسترشدا متحيرا

THALABI:v4p163/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p163/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p163/r3.claim: In a report through Ali ibn Abi Talha, Ibn Abbas says Ibrahim worshipped the star, moon, and sun until each set, then asked for guidance and disavowed shirk.
THALABI:v4p163/r3.anchor: يدل عليه ما روى علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال: لما جن عليه الليل رأى كوكبا

THALABI:v4p163/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p163/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p163/r4.claim: Other scholars reject that account because a prophet cannot pass through a time without monotheism, knowledge, or disavowal of every other object of worship.
THALABI:v4p163/r4.anchor: وأنكر الآخرون هذا القول، وقالوا: غير جائز أن يكون لله عز وجل رسول

THALABI:v4p163/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p163/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p163/r5.claim: They argue Ibrahim already had divinely granted right guidance and a pure heart, and had been shown the kingdom of heaven and earth; literal belief in a star as God is impossible.
THALABI:v4p163/r5.anchor: وأراه ملكوته فقال: إذ جاء ربه بقلب سليم وقال وكذلك نري إبراهيم ملكوت

THALABI:v4p163/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p163/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p163/r6.claim: The first of four interpretations is that Ibrahim feigned agreement with star-worshippers to expose their error: setting revealed the celestial bodies’ incapacity, although his people revered and consulted them.
THALABI:v4p163/r6.anchor: الوجه الأول: أن إبراهيم (عليه السلام) أراد أن يستدرجهم بهذا القول ويعرفهم خطأهم

THALABI:v4p163/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p163/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p163/r7.claim: An analogy begins with a visitor to idol-worshippers who feigned reverence for their idol to gain their confidence and later expose their error.
THALABI:v4p163/r7.anchor: ومثل هذا مثل الجواري الذي ورد على قوم يعبدون بدا لهم وهو الصنم

THALABI:v4p164/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p164/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p164/r1.claim: A further interpretation treats ‘this is my lord’ as an argument from the opponents’ own assumptions: the star sets, and the moon is greater, so their worship is untenable.
THALABI:v4p164/r1.anchor: والوجه الثالث: أن إبراهيم (عليه السلام) قال هذا على وجه الاحتجاج على قومه لا على معنى الشك في ربه

THALABI:v4p164/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p164/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p164/r2.claim: The account uses ellipsis: Ibrahim means ‘they say this is my lord’; as with the prayer after Abraham and Ishmael raised the House’s foundations.
THALABI:v4p164/r2.anchor: في الآية اختصار وإضمار ومعناها قال: يقولون هذا ربي كقوله وإذ يرفع إبراهيم القواعد من البيت

THALABI:v4p164/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p164/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p164/r3.claim: Ibrahim rejects a lord that disappears at setting, then repeats the argument for the moon and sun; the sun’s greater brightness makes its disappearance still clearer.
THALABI:v4p164/r3.anchor: فلما أفل غاب وزال قال: لا أحب الآفلين ربا، لا يدوم

ELMALILI:6:75-82/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r4.claim: Abraham’s words “this is my Lord” on seeing a star first serve as a taunt to those around him, questioning whether a star could nurture a human being.
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r4.anchor: Evvelâ bir yıldızın bir insanı terbiye edebileceğini istib‘âd ederek etrafındakilere bir târiz yaptı.

ELMALILI:6:75-82/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r5.claim: By saying he does not love those that set, Abraham teaches that love grounds lordship and worship, while motion and setting show createdness, subjection, change, and perishability; the true Lord creates, acts, and is free from extinction.
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r5.anchor: rubûbiyet ve ubûdiyette mahabbetin üssü’l-esâs olduğunu

ELMALILI:6:75-82/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r6.claim: The argument about setting also exposes the contradiction of replacing setting stars with idols: if the original star is inadequate, its fashioned image is even less worthy.
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r6.anchor: ufûllerinden dolayı asıllarının kâfi olmadığını teslim ettikleri hâlde

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.claim: The reference to Abraham and later prophets asserts that they invited people to Muhammad’s same message; Muhammad must follow their guidance and leave rejecters to themselves, since he must preach but cannot force belief.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.anchor: His responsibility is to only preach and he is not liable to force people to accept guidance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.claim: Abraham is singled out because Israelites and Ishmaelites both claimed him as patriarch and guide while attributing their inherited religious practices to him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.anchor: both the Israelites and the Ishmaelites regarded him as their patriarch and spiritual leader.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.claim: Judaism, Christianity, and Ishmaelite polytheism are later fabrications with no connection to Abraham; Muhammad’s mission revives and completes Abraham’s religion for his descendants.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.anchor: it was also essential to make it evident to the Ishmaelites that the religion of polytheism they have adopted is their own fabrication

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p63/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p63/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p63/.claim: The account of Abraham’s observation of the star, moon, and sun expands the earlier brief statement: their submission to divine laws shows that only their Creator deserves worship.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p63/.anchor: they explain the brevity found in the previous verses. Previously, it was stated how Abraham (sws) exposed the hollow nature of the religion followed by his father and his nation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.claim: Prophets share a preaching purpose but adjust style to their audience and temperament; John and Jesus use parables, while other prophets may sermonize or use legal diction.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.anchor: owing to the peculiar temperament and nature of their addressees, every prophet has some distinctive features with regard to his style of preaching and methodology of reasoning.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.claim: Abraham’s argumentative audience often refused to listen and quickly turned to polemics, so he used gradual reasoning to lead them into a position where they had no answer.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.anchor: Abraham’s nation was very inclined to polemical debates and argumentation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.claim: The idol-smashing episode exemplifies Abraham’s method: he directed people to ask the surviving idol and its victims, eliciting their admission that idols cannot speak or defend themselves.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.anchor: He also gestured towards the shattered idols and asked them to inquire from these victims because if they speak, they will narrate what calamity befell them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.claim: Abraham also used turiya: a true statement that can mislead listeners until his plan has unfolded; Islahi postpones its fuller example and lexical discussion to al-Saffat.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.anchor: As per this device, in order to carry out his plan, he would give a statement that would be true but could potentially mislead his addressees.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.claim: Gradual reasoning and turiya may be punctuated with polite humor; light humor is also a prophetic trait, with examples to come in al-Anbiya and al-Saffat.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.anchor: light and polite humour is also a trait of prophets of God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.claim: Abraham may have seen Venus or another star and said “This is my Lord” aloud as self-talk that listeners could hear, allowing him to raise doubt without directly provoking them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.anchor: It is possible that this be Venus or could be some other. He said that this was his Lord.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.claim: The star episode draws attention to both rising and setting: regular disappearance shows the heavenly bodies are governed, and the audience was prompted to question their inherited belief.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.anchor: When they set after rising and go after coming and that too with such punctuality that there is not the slightest change in their direction, time and shape, then they by their very existence they show that they are being governed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.claim: Abraham presents the Creator’s relation with worshippers as love rather than mere fear; fading heavenly objects are themselves subservient and cannot merit that love.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.anchor: a person’s relationship with his creator and master is that of love and not mere fear.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.claim: The author describes prophetic revelation as light upon light and refers readers to 24:35 for fuller discussion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.anchor: darkness but of light upon light.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.claim: Prophets begin by inviting their closest relatives; Abraham first invited his father before addressing his nation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.anchor: He first invited his father and this precisely has been the way of prophets of

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.claim: Abraham's argument from the celestial kingdom came after his appointment: prophets first invite their closest relatives, then address their nation, and 6:79–80 speaks with prophetic authority.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.anchor: The proof that this incident took place after Abraham (sws) was made a prophet is found in verses 79-80.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.claim: Treating the episode as an intellectual journey produces an illogical sequence: the small star appears first, while a cave story was invented to explain why Abraham saw Venus before the sun.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.anchor: A more illogical narrative had to be fabricated to justify this illogical sequence of observation:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.claim: Gradual argument accepts an opponent's premise to trap him, not to endorse it; Abraham uses the celestial bodies' setting to defeat their claim that their shining proves divinity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.anchor: if their shine is the proof of their divinity, then they should also witness their setting and fading away.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.claim: Prophets use natural, context-sensitive methods including gradual reasoning, humor, sarcasm, and double meanings; an apparently affectionate pause or sarcasm can persuade beyond many arguments.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.anchor: These include gradual reasoning, humour, sarcasm, using words and sentences with double-meaning etc.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p70/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p70/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p70/.claim: Using one's intellect and innate capacities lifts celestial bodies above idols made by human hands; neglecting them leads to worshipping carved rocks.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p70/.anchor: if a person does not use his intellect and innate abilities, he ends up prostrating before rocks he has carved out

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r1.speaker: ذو الرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r1.claim: Dhu al-Rumma’s poem compares lights in the sky with lamps, clarifying language about setting or disappearing stars.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r1.anchor: وقال ذو الرمة: مصابيح ليست باللواتي يقودها ... نجوم ولا بالآفلات الدوالك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba says القمر is the familiar moon; the root suggests whiteness, and a bright night is قمراء.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r2.anchor: القمر معروف يسمى بذلك لبياضه والأقمر الأبيض وليلة قمراء مضيئة قاله ابن قتيبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p562/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p562/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p562/r14.claim: Abraham’s condemnation of idolatry proves his guidance: “this is my Lord” is a concession to the opponent, exposing the impossibility of a changing, setting body as deity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p562/r14.anchor: وهذا الإنكار من إبراهيم على أبيه والإخبار أنه وقومه في ضلال مبين أدل دليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the star Abraham saw as Venus.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r3.anchor: والكوكب الزهرة، قاله ابن عباس وقتادة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r4.claim: Mujahid identifies the star Abraham saw as Jupiter; al-Baḥr notes its unusual quadriliteral morphology and pattern.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r4.anchor: أو المشتري، قاله مجاهد والسدي وهو رباعي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r5.claim: The apparent reply to “when night covered him” is “he saw a star”; “this is my lord” is then either an awkward adjective or, more plausibly, a new sentence. Alternatively it is the reply, with seeing as a circumstantial clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن جواب لما رأى كوكبا وعلى هذا جوزوا في قال هذا ربي أن يكون نعتا للكوكب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r6.claim: Some read “this is my lord” as a reproachful question with the interrogative hamza elided; Ibn al-Anbari calls that elision anomalous because a distinguishing cue is normally needed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r6.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: وهذا شاذ لأنه لا يجوز أن يحذف الحرف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r7.claim: A literal, committed claim that the star is God would contradict prophetic protection from sin and shirk; the childhood-worship account attributed to Ibn Abbas may be unsound, and claims that it happened after maturity are baseless.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r7.anchor: فيستحيل عليه أن يكون هذا الإخبار على سبيل الاعتقاد والتصميم لعصمة الأنبياء من المعاصي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r8.claim: A report says Abraham saw and worshiped the star, moon, and sun in childhood before each set; Abū Ḥayyān says the report may not be authentic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r8.anchor: وما روي عن ابن عباس أن ذلك وقع له في حال صباه وقبل بلوغه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the wording as a fair-minded opponent's quotation of the other side, followed by a proof that invalidates it; this draws people toward truth without partisan disputation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r9.anchor: هذا ربي قول من ينصف خصمه مع علمه أنه مبطل فيحكي قوله كما هو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari sees Abraham’s apparent agreement as a stratagem to expose the argument, like his outwardly joining the star-watchers before saying he was ill.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p564/r10.anchor: فيكون هذا القول منه استدراجا لإظهار الحجة وتوسلا إليها كما توسل إلى كسر الأصنام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r1.claim: Abraham rejects worship of bodies that set, change state, move, or disappear behind a veil, since these are properties of corporeal objects.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r1.anchor: لا أحب عبادة الآفلين المتغيرين عن حال إلى حال المنتقلين من مكان إلى مكان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r2.claim: Setting is a clearer proof than rising because it includes concealment; the plural “those that set” stresses that many stars share the trait, leaving this one with no claim to worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r2.anchor: وجاء بلفظ الآفلين ليدل على أن ثم آفلين كثيرين ساواهم هذا الكوكب في الأفول

BURSEVI:v3p44/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p44/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p44/r3.claim: The star became visible only after the sun’s light had disappeared from sight, explaining the response to “when night covered him.”
BURSEVI:v3p44/r3.anchor: جواب لما فإن رؤيته إنما تحقق بزوال نور الشمس عن الحس

BURSEVI:v3p44/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p44/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p44/r4.claim: Bursevi says this was not the star’s first rising but its disappearance against sunlight, and concludes it was near setting.
BURSEVI:v3p44/r4.anchor: وهذا صريح في أنه لم يكن في ابتداء الطلوع بل كان غيبته عن الحس بطريق الاضمحلال بنور الشمس والتحقيق إنه كان قريبا من الغروب

BURSEVI:v3p44/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p44/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p44/r5.claim: Unspecified commentators identify the star as either Venus or Jupiter, both among the seven planets.
BURSEVI:v3p44/r5.anchor: قيل كان ذلك هو الزهرة وقيل هو المشتري وكلاهما من الكواكب السبعة السيارة

BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r1.claim: Ibrahim speaks as though agreeing with his opponents, presenting their claim on its own terms before refuting it.
BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r1.anchor: قال على سبيل الموافقة مع الخصم

BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r2.claim: Ibrahim’s father and people worshiped idols and celestial bodies; an opponent’s claim can be recited from his own viewpoint and then refuted.
BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r2.anchor: وكان أبوه وقومه يعبدون الأصنام والكواكب والمستدل على فساد قول يحكيه على رأي خصمه ثم يكر عليه بالإبطال

BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r3.claim: Setting lords move between places and states and disappear behind veils, so they cannot deserve lordship.
BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r3.anchor: أي : الأرباب المنتقلين من مكان إلى مكان المتغيرين من حال إلى حال المحتجبين بالأستار فإنهم بمعزل عن استحقاق الربوبية قطعا

BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r1.claim: A Persian account says Ibrahim appeared mature at eighteen months, matching eighteen-year-olds, while reports place his cave years at ages thirteen or seventeen.
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r1.anchor: ون انزده ماهه شد باجوانان انزده ساله مقابل كشت وازخانه بيرون آمد وكفته اند هفت سال باسيزده سال يا هفتده سال درغار بود

BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r2.claim: A relative told Azer the earlier report of Ibrahim’s death was false, then showed him the handsome, well-mannered youth in the cave.
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r2.anchor: جواني رسيده است درغايت خوب رويى ونيكو خويى س آزررا بغار آورد وإبراهيم را بوي نمود

BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r3.claim: Azer was delighted by Ibrahim’s beauty and was told to bring him from the cave to serve Nimrod.
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r3.anchor: اين را ازغار بخانه آوركه بملازمت نمرود بريم

BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r4.claim: Seeing the animals, Ibrahim asks his mother who creates and provides for them.
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r4.anchor: إبراهيم ازمادر رسيدكه هر آيينه اين هارا رورد كارى خواهد بودكه آفريده وروزي ميدهد

BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r5.claim: His mother says she provides for him and names Nimrod as her own provider; Ibrahim asks who is Nimrod’s God, and she scolds him for dangerous talk.
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r5.anchor: ما درش كفت من روردكار توام إبراهيم كفت روردكار توكيست

BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r6.claim: In Nimrod’s time some people worshiped stars, sun, and moon, others idols, and others Nimrod.
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r6.anchor: در زمان نمرود بعضي ستاره وآفتاب وماه مي رستيدند وبرخى بت رست بودند وجمعي رستش نمرود مى كردند

BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r7.claim: Star worshipers bow when Ibrahim sees the star; his “this is my lord” is read as a question or as speaking from their belief.
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r7.anchor: س بعضي كه ستاره رست بودندي روى بوي سجده كردند {قال هاذا ربى} أي اينست روردكار من بر سبيل استفهام يا بزعم آن قوم

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r1.claim: Abraham, dated to around 2100 BCE and regarded as leader of the monotheistic Hanif tradition, lived among people who worshipped celestial bodies and their idol symbols.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r1.anchor: Milâttan önce 2100’lerde yaşadığı kabul edilen ve Allah’ın birliği esasına dayalı dinî geleneğin (Hanîflik) önderi olarak bilinen Hz. İbrâhim’in kavmi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r2.claim: According to the Torah, tablets found in excavations at Abraham's birthplace, Ur, mention about five thousand divine names.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r2.anchor: Tevrat’a göre Hz. İbrâhim’in doğum yeri olan Ur şehrinde yapılan kazılar sonucu bulunan tabletlerde 5000 civarında tanrı ismi geçmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r3.claim: Abraham was probably already a monotheist before these observations; he considered a star, then the moon and sun, to persuade his people from within their false beliefs.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r3.anchor: muhtemelen kendisi bu gözlemlere girişmeden önce de tevhid ehlinden olmakla birlikte, kavminin bu bâtıl inançlarından hareket ederek onları tevhid akîdesine ikna etmek düşüncesiyle

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r4.claim: His argument is that transient, changing beings cannot be gods or objects of divine love, so none of the celestial bodies is divine and only God is truly worthy of worship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r4.anchor: gelip geçici ve değişken bir varlığın tanrı olamayacağı, tanrısal bir sevgiyle benimsenemeyeceği şeklindeki temel gerçeğe dayanarak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r5.claim: Abraham's declaration of certain faith culminates in turning as a hanif to the Creator of heaven and earth and disavowing associationism; his observational reasoning refutes idolatry and demonstrates proper belief in God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r5.anchor: “Ben, Hanîf olarak yüzümü, gökleri ve yeri yoktan yaratana çevirdim ve ben müşriklerden değilim” ifadesiyle ortaya koymuştur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r8.claim: The Qur'an's main struggle is against associationism rather than outright atheism because it regards the idea of divinity as innate and corrupted by polytheism and other forms of shirk.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r8.anchor: Kur’an’ın temel tavrı, tanrı tanımazlardan ziyade şirkle mücadeledir.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم في رواية حفص
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and Hafs from Asim open both rāʾ and hamza in رأى كوكبا.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وعاصم في رواية حفص، رأى بفتح الراء والهمزة

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r2.speaker: نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r2.claim: Nafi reads the two vowels between opening and kasra; Al-Farisi says this may refer to hamza alone or to both rāʾ and hamza.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r3.claim: Abu Amr opens rāʾ and breaks hamza; another transmission from him through al-Qutai and Ubayd ibn Aqil breaks both.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو: رأى كوكبا بفتح الراء وكسر الهمزة

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r4.speaker: القطعي عن عبيد بن عقيل عن أبي عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r4.claim: This transmission from Abu Amr breaks both rāʾ and hamza.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r4.anchor: وروى القطعي عن عبيد بن عقيل عن أبي عمرو: بكسر الراء والهمزة جميعا

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r5.speaker: عاصم في رواية أبي بكر وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r5.claim: Abu Bakr from Asim, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisai break both rāʾ and hamza.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r5.anchor:
وقرأ عاصم في رواية أبي بكر وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
رأى* بكسر الراء والهمزة

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r6.claim: Readers without imala leave both the alif and its preceding vowel unaffected, as in رعى and رمى; readers incline the preceding fatha to incline the alif toward yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r6.anchor: أنهما لم يميلا، كما أن من قال: رعى ورمى لما لم يمل الألف لم يمل الفتحة التي قبلها

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r7.claim: Nafi’s intermediate reading may incline only hamza’s fatha to draw the alif toward yāʾ, or incline both vowels, with rāʾ following hamza’s imala by analogy to adjacent imalas.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r7.anchor: فإن كان يريد فتحة الهمزة فإنما أمالها نحو الكسرة لتميل الألف التي في رأى نحو الياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r8.claim: When both vowels are inclined, the rāʾ fatha follows hamza’s imala, like the fatha in رأيت عمادا following the inclined alif.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r8.anchor: وأما إمالة الفتحة التي على الراء، فإنما أمالها لاتباعه إياها إمالة فتحة الهمزة

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r9.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r9.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r9.claim: Breaking rāʾ is justified because the imperfect is على يفعل, suggesting a past pattern على فعل; the guttural hamza then triggers kasra on the first radical.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p326#2/r9.anchor: قال : وجه قراءتهم أنهم كسروا الراء من رأى، لأن المضارع منه على يفعل، وإذا كان المضارع على «يفعل» فكأن الماضي على «فعل»

QASHANI:6:76-77/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:76-77/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:76-77/r1.claim: The night is the darkness of bodily nature during childhood and early youth.
QASHANI:6:76-77/r1.anchor: أظلم عليه ليل عالم الطبيعة الجسمانية في صباه وأول شبابه

QASHANI:6:76-77/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:76-77/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:76-77/r2.claim: The star signifies the angelic realm of the human structure, namely the soul as spiritual spirit; Abraham experiences its life and lordship as God manifests through the name al-Muḥyī.
QASHANI:6:76-77/r2.anchor: كوكب ملكوت الهيكل الإنساني التي هي النفس المسماة روحا روحانية وجد فيضه وحياته وربوبيته منها

QASHANI:6:76-77/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:76-77/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:76-77/r3.claim: The star's setting is the soul's passing from its station as the heart's light rises; recognizing the soul's contingency and bodily dependence, Abraham rejects what is veiled by the body and needy of another.
QASHANI:6:76-77/r3.anchor: بعبوره عن مقام النفس وطلوع نور القلب وإشراقه عليه بآثار الرشد والتعقل ومعرفته لإمكان النفس

ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r1.claim: The clause when night covered him may connect to when Abraham said, with the intervening material serving as a parenthesis supporting what precedes and follows.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r1.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون عطفا على ( إد قال إبراهيم ) وما بينهما اعتراض مقرر لما سبق ولحق

ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r2.claim: Abraham’s recognition that God owns and rules the heavens, earth, and all within them, that all are subject to and depend on Him, and that Abraham had reached certainty rules out the divinity of anything else, including his people’s idols and planets; some investigators prefer this reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r2.anchor: فان تعريفه عليه السلام ربوبيته ومالكيته تعالى للسموات والأرض وما فيهن وكون الكل مقهورا تحت ملكوته مفتقرا اليه عز شأنه في جميع أحواله وكونه من الراسخين في المعرفة الواصلين إلى ذروة عين اليقين مما يقتضي بان يحكم باستحالة ألوهية ما سواه سبحانه من الأصنام والكواكب التي كان يعبدوها قومه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r3.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r3.claim: Some careful scholars prefer connecting the night clause to the earlier when Abraham said rather than treating it as a new elaboration.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r4.claim: Alternatively, the verse details the previously summarized views of the kingdom and explains how Abraham reasoned his way to certainty; the order reflects detail narrated after summary.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون تفصيلا لما ذكر من آراء الملوت وبيانا لكيفية استلاله عليه السلام ووصوله إلى رتبة الايقان والترتيب ذكرى لتأخر التفصيل عن الاجمال في الذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r5.claim: Janna means to cover with darkness; derivatives of the root convey concealment.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r5.anchor: ومعنى ( فلما جن عليه الليل ) ستره بظلامه وهذ المادة بمتصرفاتها تدل على الستر

ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r6.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r6.claim: Al-Rāghib says the root j-n-n originally means concealment from the senses and explains the related forms for night covering or providing a covering.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198/r6.anchor: وعن الراغب أصل الجن الستر عن الحاسة يقال : جنه الليل وأجنه وجن عليه فجنه وجن عليه ستره وأجنه جعل له ما يستره

ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r1.speaker: شيخ الاسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r1.claim: The sighting occurred after sunlight had made the star disappear, likely near its setting, rather than at its first rising.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r1.anchor: وهذا كما قال شيخ الاسلام صريح في أنه لم يكن في ابتداء الطلوع بل كان بعد غيبته عن الحس بطريق الاضمحلال بنور الشمس والتحقيق عنده أنه كان قريبا من الغروب

ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the star Abraham saw as Jupiter.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r2.anchor: والمراد بالكوكب فيما روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما المشتري

ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r3.claim: Qatada reports that the star was Venus.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر وغيره عن قتادة أنه قال : ذكر لنا أنه الزهرة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r4.claim: Al-Alusi reads “this is my Lord” as a provisional concession in argument: Abraham adopts his father’s and people’s premise so he can refute it, as debaters recount an opponent’s claim before disproving it.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r4.anchor: استئناف مبني على سؤال نشأ من الكلام السابق وهدا منه عليه السلام على سبيل الفرض وارخاء العنان مجاراة مع أبيه وقومه الذين كانوا يعبدون الأصنام والكواكب فان المستدل على فساد قول يحكيه ثم يكر عليه بالابطال

ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r5.claim: An alternative parses the words as a repudiating question with its interrogative particle omitted, a common Arabic usage illustrated by poetry and Qur’anic examples.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : إن في الكلام استفهاما إنكاريا محذوفا وحذف أداة الاستفهام كثير في كلامهم ومنه قوله : ثم قالوا تحبها قلت بهرا وقوله : فقلت وأنكرت الوجوه هم هم وروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال في قوله تعالى : ( فلا اقتحم العقبة ) إن المعنى أفلا اقتحم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r6.claim: Another alternative takes the statement as sarcasm, like ironically calling a lowly person the chief of a people.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r6.anchor: وقيل : انه مقول على سبيل الاستهزاء كما يقال لذليل ساد قوما : هذا سيدكم على سبيل الاستهزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r7.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r7.claim: The Imam says Abraham feigned agreement because his people’s inherited beliefs made direct preaching futile; his heart remained faithful, and this seeming concession secured a hearing for the proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r7.anchor: وقيل : إنه عليه السلام أراد أن يبطل قولهم بربوبية الكواكب إلا أنه عليه السلام كان قد عرف من تقليدهم لأسلافهم وبعد طباعهم عن قبول الدلائل أنه لو صرح بالدعوة إلى الله تعالى لم يقبلوا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r8.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r8.claim: The Imam argues that if coercion permits speaking unbelief to save oneself, it is more justified to appear to agree in order to rescue a whole community from disbelief and eternal punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r8.anchor: لما لم يجد إلى الدعوة طريقا سوى هذا الطريق وكان مأمورا بالدعوة إلى الله تعالى كان بمنزلة المكره على كلمة الكفر ومعلوم أنه عند الاكراه يجوز إجراء كلمة الكفر على اللسان

ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r9.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r9.claim: He supports this interpretation by comparing Abraham’s apparent cooperation with astrologers to his statement that he was sick, which let him reach his aim of breaking the idols.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r9.anchor: ومما يقوي هذا القول أنه تعالى حكى عنه مثل هذا الطريق في موضع آخر وهو قوله تعالى فنظر نظرة في النجوم فقال إني سقيم وذلك لأن القوم كانوا يستدلون بعلم النجوم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r10.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r10.claim: Another report says that, while the people were debating and inviting Abraham to worship the planets, he pointed to the rising star as the very Lord they urged him to worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r10.anchor: وقيل : إن القوم بينما كانوا يدعونه عليه السلام إلى عبادة النجوم وكانت المناظرة بينهم قائمة على ساق إذ طلع النجم فقال : ( هذا ربي ) على معنى هذا هو الرب الذي تدعونني اليه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r11.claim: Al-Alusi rejects these accounts, especially the Imam’s, because they assume the statement came after Abraham’s maturity and call to monotheism, which the passage’s sequence supports.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p198#2/r11.anchor: والكل ليس بشيء عند المحققين لا سيما ما قرره الامام وتلك الأقوال كلها مبنية على أن هذا القول كان بعد البلوغ ودعوة القوم إلى التوحيد وسياق الآية وسباقها شاهدا عدل على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r1.claim: Some claim the scene preceded puberty and was a hypothetical reductio after Abraham already believed in God, so no doubt leading to unbelief was involved; Al-Alusi says this is contrary to the apparent context.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r1.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أنه كان قبل البلوغ ولا يلزمه اختلاج شك مؤد إلى كفر لأنه لما آمن بالغيب أراد أن يؤيد ما جزم به بأنه لو لم يكن الله تعالى إلها

ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r2.claim: Another claim says Abraham spoke without knowing God, but childhood ignorance before proof does no harm and is not unbelief; Al-Alusi dismisses this outright.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r2.anchor: وزعم أنه عليه السلام قال ما قال إد لم يكن عارفا بربه سبحانه والجهل حال الطفولية قبل قيام الحجة لا يضر ولا يعد ذلك كفرا مما لا يلتفت اليه أصلا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r3.speaker: المحققون
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r3.claim: The established scholars hold that a prophet is never without knowledge of and devotion to God, and is always free of worshipping anything else; Abraham’s childhood story confirms this especially clearly.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r3.anchor: فقد قال المحققون المحقون : إنه لا يجوز أن يكون لله تعالى رسول يأتي عليه وقت من الاوقات إلا وهو لله تعالى موحد وبه عارف ومن كل معبود سواه بريء وقد قص الله تعالى من حال إبراهيم عليه السلام خصوصا في صغره

ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r4.claim: Al-Alusi says the valid explanation is the earlier argumentative one; stellar divinity is subtler to refute than idol worship, so blunt denial at the outset would have provoked obstinacy.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r4.anchor: فالوجه الأول لا غير ولعل سلوك تلك الطريقة في بيان استحالة ربوبية الكوكب دون بيان استحالة إلهية الأصنام كما قيل لما أن هذا أخفى بطلانا واستحالة من الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r5.claim: Some say the people worshipped planets through metal idols assigned to them, such as gold for the sun and silver for the moon; Abraham first denied the idols, then their celestial sources.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r5.anchor: وقيل : إن القوم كانوا يعبدون الكواكب فاتخذؤا لكل كوكب صنما من المعادن المنسوبة اليه كالذهب للشمس والفضة للقمر ليتقربوا اليها فكان الصنم كالقبلة لهم فأنكر أولا عبادتهم للاصنام بحسب الظاهر ثم أبطل منشآتها

ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r6.claim: This account adds that the people may have regarded the planets as independently effective, unlike the idols, which explains Abraham’s separate challenge to their divinity and lordship.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r6.anchor: ولعلهم كانوا يعتقدون تأثيرها إستقلالا دون تأثير الأصنام ولهذا تعرض لبطلان الالهية في الأصنام والربوبية فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو وورش من طريق البخاري؛ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وخلف ويحيى عن أبي بكر
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r7.claim: Abu Amr and Warsh through al-Bukhari read رأى with fatḥa on rāʾ and kasra on hamza; Ibn Amir, Hamza, al-Kisai, Khalaf, and Yahya from Abu Bakr read it with both letters kasra-marked.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p199/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وورش من طريق البخاري رأى بفتح الراء وكسر الهمزة حيث كان وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وخلف ويحيى عن أبي بكر رأئى بسر الراء والهمزة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p200/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200/r1.claim: The setting bodies are described as moving between places and changing states; the denial of love points to denying their divinity, or, by ellipsis, to refusing worship of them.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200/r1.anchor: اي الأرباب المنتقلين من مكان إلى مكان المتغيرين من حال إلى حال ونفي لمحبة قيل إشارة إلى نفي اعتقاد الربوبية الكلام مضافا أي لا أحب عبادة الآفلين

ALUSI-FULL:v7p200/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200/r2.claim: Their movement and disappearance entail origination and contingency, which are impossible for the eternal Lord and worshipped deity.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200/r2.anchor: فمبتدأ الاشتقاق علة للحكم لأن الأقوال انتقال واحتجاب وكل منها ينافي استحقاق الربوبية والألوهية التي هي من مقتضيات الربوبية لاقتضاء ذلك الحدوث والامكان المستحيلين على الرب المعبود القديم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r1.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r1.claim: Unattributed reports say Abraham remained in the cave for seven, thirteen, or seventeen years.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r1.anchor: وقيل: إنه كان في السرب سبع سنين، وقيل: ثلاثة عشرة سنة، وقيل: سبعة عشرة سنة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r2.claim: One account says the young Abraham questioned his mother, father, and Nimrod about who created them; after the adults silenced him, he saw a star through the cave opening and called it his lord.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r2.anchor: فلطمه لطمة وقال له: اسكت فلما جن عليه الليل دنا من باب السرب فنظر من خلال الصخرة فأبصر كوكبا، قال: هذا ربي.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r3.claim: Another account says Abraham asked his parents to take him outside, inferred that the camels, horses, and sheep must have a creator, and then saw the evening star.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r3.anchor: ويقال: إنه قال لأبويه أخرجاني فأخرجاه من السرب وانطلقا به حين غابت الشمس، فنظر إبراهيم إلى الإبل والخيل والغنم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r4.claim: The star was Jupiter or, according to another report, Venus; since the moon rose late at the end of the month, Abraham saw the star before it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r4.anchor: ثم نظر فإذا المشتري قد طلع، ويقال: الزهرة، وكانت تلك الليلة في آخر الشهر فتأخر طلوع القمر فيها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r5.claim: Janna ʿalayhi al-layl means night came on, darkened, and covered everything; the listed Arabic forms share this sense, and junūn al-layl means its blackness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r5.anchor: يقال: جن الليل وأجن الليل، وجنه الليل، وأجن عليه الليل يجن جنونا وجنانا إذا أظلم وغطى كل شيء،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r6.claim: Readers differ in the vocalization of raʾā: Abū ʿAmr opens rāʾ and kasras alif, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, and Abū Bakr kasra both; further contexts alter some readers' forms.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r6.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو (رأى) بفتح الراء وكسر الألف، وبكسرهما ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r7.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r7.claim: Some take Abraham's statement at face value: he was searching for monotheism until God guided him, and his statement did not harm his reasoning because it was before the proof bound him in childhood, not unbelief.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p161/r7.anchor: واختلفوا في قوله ذلك: فأجراه بعضهم على الظاهر، وقالوا: كان إبراهيم عليه السلام مسترشدا طالبا للتوحيد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p162/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p162/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p162/r1.claim: A fourth interpretation supplies an omitted they say before this is my lord, as in the verse about Abraham and Ishmael raising the House's foundations, where they say our Lord, accept from us.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p162/r1.anchor: والوجه الرابع: فيه إضمار وتقديره يقولون هذا ربي، كقوله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p162/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p162/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p162/r2.claim: Afala means set; Abraham says he does not love what does not endure.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p162/r2.anchor: {فلما أفل قال لا أحب الآفلين} وما لا يدوم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r1.claim: The account details the preceding point.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r2.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r2.claim: Alternatively, the clause is joined to Abraham's speech, while “thus We show” is parenthetical.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r2.anchor: وقيل عطف على قال إبراهيم وكذلك نري اعتراض

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r3.claim: Because Abraham's father and people worshiped idols and celestial bodies, he aimed to expose their error and guide them through reasoning.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r3.anchor: فإن أباه وقومه كانوا يعبدون الأصنام والكواكب، فأراد أن ينبههم على ضلالتهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r4.claim: The night's covering means darkness covered him; the star was either Venus or Jupiter.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r4.anchor: وجن عليه الليل ستره بظلامه والكواكب كان الزهرة أو المشتري

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r5.claim: “This is my lord” may stage an opponent's claim so Abraham can refute it, or express genuine inquiry and reasoning; he said it in adolescence or near puberty.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r5.anchor: على سبيل الوضع فإن المستدل على فساد قول يحكيه على ما يقوله الخصم ثم يكر عليه بالإفساد،

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r6.claim: Afala means that the star set or disappeared.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r6.anchor: أي غاب. { قال لا أحب الآفلين } فضلا عن عبادتهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r7.claim: He would not love celestial bodies, much less worship them, because setting and concealment indicate transience and origination, incompatible with divinity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:76/r7.anchor: فضلا عن عبادتهم فإن الانتقال والاحتجاب بالأستار يقتضي الأمان والحدوث وينافي الألوهية

SULAMI:v1p205/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p205/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p205/r1.claim: Some describe the inward cosmos as filled with stars, suns, and moons of unity, overcoming doubts stirred by the visible celestial lights.
SULAMI:v1p205/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : كمن فيه كواكب الوحدانية وشموسها وأقمارها

SULAMI:v1p205/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p205/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p205/r2.claim: Al-Wasiti says Abraham saw the Real through his innermost secret, rather than seeing the star itself.
SULAMI:v1p205/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : في قوله رأى كوكبا قال : إنه كان يطالع الحق بسره لا الكواكب

SULAMI:v1p205/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p205/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p205/r3.claim: Al-Wasiti reads dislike of setting as grief at losing the state of witnessing that had absorbed and made Abraham present to God.
SULAMI:v1p205/r3.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : في قوله رأى كوكبا قال : إنه كان يطالع الحق بسره لا الكواكب ، وكذلك في الشمس والقمر

SULAMI:v1p205/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p205/r4.speaker: النصرآباذي
SULAMI:v1p205/r4.claim: Al-Nasrabadi says Abraham saw setting outwardly in created branches and, at the roots, saw setting itself and its nullity; this made him yearn for the One who never sets, as his poem contrasts the setting sun with the heart's sun that never disappears.
SULAMI:v1p205/r4.anchor: وقال النصرآباذي : أراه بالفرع الأفول وأراه في الأصول نفس الأفول وبطلانه فقال : ﴿ لا أحب الآفلين ﴾ . وقال أيضا : أراه الأفول حتى هيمه فيمن

SULAMI:v1p205/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p205/r5.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p205/r5.claim: Ibn Ata reads the first statement as distinguishing Abraham from his people and the next as seeking increased guidance; once the proof was established, Abraham disavowed their associations.
SULAMI:v1p205/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطاء في هذه الآية ﴿ هذا ربي ﴾ قال : كان الأول تفريقا للقوم ، والثاني مسأله الإزدياد للهداية

SULAMI:v1p205/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p205/r6.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p205/r6.claim: The fading heavenly body proves the Lord is eternal and unchanging; what depends on itself, occupies places, and departs from them cannot be Lord.
SULAMI:v1p205/r6.anchor: وقيل هذا دليل على ربي ، لأن ربي لم يزل ولا يزال ولا يزول وهذا آفل

SULAMI:v1p205/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p205/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p205/r7.claim: One account traces Abraham's passage from darkness and compulsion through lights of lordship and awe, to effacement of human traits, subsistence in the Everlasting, and disavowal of association.
SULAMI:v1p205/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لما أظلم عليه الكون وعمى عن الإختيار وألجأه الإضطرار إلى النفس

SULAMI:v1p206/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p206/r7.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p206/r7.claim: Ibn Ata says Abraham's intense love and longing made him lose sight of created traces and cling to their Maker; this is the station of union, in which he sees and mentions none besides God.
SULAMI:v1p206/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطاء في قوله : ^ ( هذا ربي ) ^ قال : كان إبراهيم صلى الله عليه وسلم من شدة حبه لربه وشغفه به

BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r4.claim: Because heavenly bodies are visible to all and nobler than earthly objects, disproving their divinity disproves the divinity of earthly objects all the more.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r4.anchor: وهي أشرف من الأرضية , فإذا بطلت صلاحيتها للإلهية بطلت الأرضية من باب الأولى

BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r5.claim: He glosses the night as covering and darkening; the shortened verb form intensifies the darkness, while the following preposition depicts night falling over Abraham.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r5.anchor: فلما جن } أي ستر وأظلم , وقصره - وإن كان متعديا - دلالة على شدة ظلام تلك الليلة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r6.claim: The star had appeared or risen when Abraham saw it.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r7.claim: Abraham's words can be read as either a statement or a question; he feigned affirmation to draw his audience into reflection and make them receptive to proof.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r7.anchor: الصالح لأن يكون خبرا واستفهاما , ليوهمهم أنه مخبر

BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r8.claim: Setting proves that a star changes and moves, so it is originated and contingent rather than divine; Abraham spoke in his own voice only to alert his audience, since God had made him certain.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r8.anchor: لأن الأفول حركة , والحركة تدل على حدوث المتحرك وإمكانه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r9.claim: He prefers setting as evidence over rising: setting more clearly signals the star's lost power and insignificance, whereas rising still carries honor and apparent authority.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r9.anchor: ولم يستدل بالطلوع لأنه - وإن كان حركة دالة على الحدوث والنقصان - شرف في الجملة وسلطان

BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r10.claim: Different audiences grasp different force in the proof: learned people infer contingency and a necessary creator, middling people infer origination from motion, and ordinary people see loss of light and authority.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r10.anchor: فالخواص يفهمون من الأفول الإمكان , والممكن لا بد له من موجد واجب الوجود

BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r11.claim: The argument also targets Abraham's Persian people, who believed a planet's influence weakens as it descends west; a true deity does not change.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r11.anchor: وخص الأفول أيضا لأن قومه الفرس كانوا منجمين , ومذهبهم أن الكوكب إذا كان صاعدا من المشرق إلى وسط السماء كان قويا عظيم التأثير

BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r12.claim: This argument shows that religion is grounded in proof rather than imitation.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p658/r12.anchor: وهذا الاستدلال برهان في أن أصل الدين مبني على الحجة دون التقليد

TUSTARI:6:75-76/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:75-76/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:6:75-76/r1.claim: Abraham's statement that the star was his lord was an indirect argument for people whose hearts were perplexed; he had already received right guidance.
TUSTARI:6:75-76/r1.anchor: كان هذا القول منه تعريضا لقومه عند حيرة قلوبهم، لأنه كان أوتي رشده من قبل

DURR-FULL:v3p304/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p304/r4.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v3p304/r4.claim: Abraham emerged after sunset, saw Jupiter and called it his lord, then rejected a lord who disappears when the star set.
DURR-FULL:v3p304/r4.anchor: فإذا هو بالكوكب وهو المشتري فقال: هذا ربي فلم يلبث أن غاب قال: لا أحب ربا يغيب

DURR-FULL:v3p306/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p306/r1.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v3p306/r1.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the star Abraham saw as Jupiter, which appears toward the direction of prayer at sunset.
DURR-FULL:v3p306/r1.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {رأى كوكبا} قال: هو المشتري وهو الذي يطلع نحو القبلة عند المغرب

DURR-FULL:v3p306/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p306/r2.speaker: زيد بن علي
DURR-FULL:v3p306/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Ali instead identifies Abraham's star as Venus.
DURR-FULL:v3p306/r2.anchor: عن زيد بن علي في قوله {رأى كوكبا} قال: الزهرة

DURR-FULL:v3p306/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p306/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p306/r4.claim: Qatada glosses those that set as things that pass away.
DURR-FULL:v3p306/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {لا أحب الآفلين} قال: الزائلين

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r1.claim: He says Abraham emerged from the cave after sunset when the night covered him.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r1.anchor: عن السدى يعني قوله : فلما جن عليه الليل راى كوكبا قال : وكان خروجه حين خرج من السرب بعد غروب الشمس

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r2.speaker: زيد بن علي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r2.claim: He identifies the star as Venus.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r2.anchor: عن زيد بن علي في قوله : فلما جن عليه الليل راى كوكبا قال : الزهرة

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r3.claim: He identifies the star as Jupiter.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r3.anchor: عن السدى ، في قول الله : فلما جن عليه الليل راى كوكبا قال : هو المشتري

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r4.claim: He says Abraham worshipped the star until it set.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قوله : راى كوكبا قال هذا ربي ، فعبده حتى غاب

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r5.claim: He says Abraham saw Jupiter, called it his lord, and soon saw it disappear.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r5.anchor: عن السدى قوله : فلما افل قال لا احب الافلين ، قال : فلما رفع راسه إلى السماء فاذا هو بالكوكب ، وهو المشتري

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله عز وجل فلما افل ، قال ذهب

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r7.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r7.claim: He glosses “I do not love those that set” as “I do not love a lord who disappears.”
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r7.anchor: عن السدى قوله : قال لا احب الافلين ، قال : لا احب ربا يغيب

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r8.claim: Qatada reports that after God showed Abraham the kingdom of the heavens, Abraham saw a star set and understood his Lord is enduring and does not pass away.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r8.anchor: عن قتادة : قوله : فلما افل قال لا احب الافلين ، ذكر لنا ان نبي الله إبراهيم صلى الله عليه وسلم بعدما اراه الله ملكوت السموات راى كوكبا

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r9.claim: He glosses “those that set” as those that pass away.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1328/r9.anchor: عن قتادة ، في قوله : لا احب الافلين ، قال : الزائلين

AKHFASH:v1p304/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p304/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p304/r1.claim: Akhfash cites the form أجن alongside جن for night falling over someone; the poems illustrate أجن and the verbal noun الجن for جن.
AKHFASH:v1p304/r1.anchor: وقال {فلما جن عليه الليل} وقال بعضهم {أجن} . وقال الشاعر: [من الطويل وهو الشاهد الرابع والتسعون بعد المئة] :

AKHFASH:v1p304/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p304/r2.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v1p304/r2.claim: An unidentified ṭawīl poem uses أجن الليل as evidence for the form أجن.
AKHFASH:v1p304/r2.anchor: فلما أجن الليل بتنا كأننا * علىكثرة الأعداء محترسان

AKHFASH:v1p304/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p304/r3.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v1p304/r3.claim: A second unidentified rajaz poem likewise attests أجنك الليل.

AKHFASH:v1p304/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p304/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p304/r4.claim: الجن can be the verbal noun of جن; alternatively أجن is sound with its own verbal noun, as in العطاء and الإعطاء.
AKHFASH:v1p304/r4.anchor: فجعل "الجن" مصدرا ل"جن". وقد يستقيم أن يكون "أجن" ويكون ذا مصدره كما قال "العطاء" و"الإعطاء".

AKHFASH:v1p304/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p304/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p304/r5.claim: For أكننتم في أنفسكم, speakers use مكنون or مكن; كننت a girl means protected her, while كننتها and أكننتها من الشمس both mean sheltered her from the sun.
AKHFASH:v1p304/r5.anchor: وأما قوله {أكننتم في أنفسكم} فإنهم يقولون في مفعولها: "مكنون" ويقول بعضهم "مكن"

AKHFASH:v1p304/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p304/r6.speaker: author
