AKHFASH:v1p304/r6.claim: Qays says كننت العلم, with passive مكنون; Banū Tamīm says أكننت العلم, with passive مكن, as in the Qur'anic examples أكننتم and بيض مكنون.
AKHFASH:v1p304/r6.anchor: لأن قيسا تقول: "كننت العلم" فهو "مكنون". [111 ء] وتقول بنو تميم "أكننت العلم" ف"هو مكن"،

AKHFASH:v1p304/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p304/r7.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v1p304/r7.claim: An unidentified basīṭ poet's phrase في الصدر مكنون is cited as evidence for Qays's passive mكنون.
AKHFASH:v1p304/r7.anchor: قد كنت أعطيهم مالي وأمنحهم * عرضي وعندهم في الصدر مكنون

AKHFASH:v1p304/r8.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p304/r8.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v1p304/r8.claim: An unidentified kāmil poet uses كن يكنن in a line about faces being concealed; Qays recites the line as قد كن يكنن.
AKHFASH:v1p304/r8.anchor: قد كن يكنن الوجوه تسترا * فاليوم حين بدون للنظار

AKHFASH:v1p304/r9.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p304/r9.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p304/r9.claim: أفل is the verb يأفل, with verbal noun أفولا.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317/r1.claim: فلما جن branches from the showing of the heavenly kingdom in 6:75, since the star belongs to that kingdom and فاء signals close derivation; al-Zamakhshari’s link to 6:74 with an intervening parenthesis is inelegant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317/r1.anchor: لأن العطف بالفاء يستدعي مزيد الاتصال بين المعطوف والمعطوف عليه لما في معنى الفاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r1.claim: جن عليه الليل means darkness enveloped Ibrahim, implying he was outdoors beneath the sky rather than inside a house.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r1.anchor: أي كان إبراهيم محوطا بظلمة الليل ، وهو يقتضي أنه كان تحت السماء ولم يكن في بيت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r2.claim: The wording يا قوم implies Ibrahim was traveling with a group of his people as they watched the celestial bodies; his Chaldean people were Sabians who worshiped stars and their images.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r2.anchor: أنه كان سائرا مع فريق من قومه يشاهدون الكواكب ، وقد كان قوم إبراهيم صابئين يعبدون الكواكب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r3.claim: جن عليه الليل intensifies the covering image, as though the darkness were a garment; the author says جن الليل was not used intransitively to mean simply that night became dark.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r3.anchor: وهذا يقصد به المبالغة في الستر بالظلمة حتى صارت كأنها غطاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r4.claim: Ibrahim likely noticed a bright, prominent star incidentally, perhaps shining near mid-sky; alternatively, the text may omit his deliberate looking, as 26:63 omits the striking of the sea.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون نظر الكواكب فرأى كوكبا فيكون في الكلام إيجاز حذف مثل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r5.speaker: زيد بن علي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Ali identifies the star as Venus.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r5.anchor: فعن زيد بن علي أن الكوكب هو الزهرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the star as Jupiter.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r7.claim: The clause رأى كوكبا is the جواب of لما.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r7.anchor: وجملة { رأى كوكبا } جواب { لما } . والكوكب : النجم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r8.claim: قال هذا ربي begins a new explanatory sentence answering the question prompted by the report that Ibrahim saw a star.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r8.anchor: وجملة : { قال هذا ربي } مستأنفة استئنافا بيانيا جوابا لسؤال ينشأ عن مضمون جملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r9.claim: The demonstrative marks something sought and investigated, then found; the author also allows its literal pointing and allusive sense together, comparing other Qur'anic uses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p317#2/r9.anchor: أن يكون القصد الأصلي منه هو الكناية بالإشارة عن كون المشار إليه أمرا مطلوبا مبحوثا عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319/r1.claim: Definite هذا ربي implies restriction: Ibrahim provisionally left one of their gods in place, feigning acceptance of one deity so his people would listen and move toward monotheism.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319/r1.anchor: فدل على أن إبراهيم عليه السلام أراد استدراج قومه فابتدأ بإظهار أنه لا يرى تعدد الآلهة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319/r2.claim: قال is literal speech addressed to others, as shown by the passage’s sequence, its direct address يا قوم, and the fact that refuting stars alone works only if they were his people’s claimed gods; Ibrahim argued before a gathered group.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319/r2.anchor: فدل ذلك كله على أن إبراهيم عليه السلام قال ذلك على سبيل المجادلة لقومه وإرخاء العنان لهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319#2/r1.claim: هذا ربي means my creator and manager, therefore one deserving worship; Ibrahim said it hypothetically in his people’s terms to draw them in before refuting their belief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319#2/r1.anchor: وقوله : { هذا ربي } أي خالقي ومدبري فهو مستحق عبادتي . قاله على سبيل الفرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319#2/r2.claim: Though it sounds like disbelief, Ibrahim could utter it without believing it if he judged this the likeliest way to guide and save his people; coerced denial with a faithful heart is an analogy, and revelation may have authorized his strategy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319#2/r2.anchor: ساغ له التصريح به لقصد الوصول إلى الحق وهو لا يعتقده ، ولا يزيد قوله هذا قومه كفرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319#2/r3.claim: The passage indicates Chaldean Sabian star worship; their idols may have represented stars, as in ancient Greek myths, or they may have worshiped stars alongside lesser images, as Greeks distinguished gods from demigods; Sabians assigned spirits to stars.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319#2/r3.anchor: وعلى هذا فالآية تقتضي أن قومه يعبدون الكواكب وأنهم على دين الصابئة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319#2/r4.claim: أفل means a celestial light disappeared by setting behind the horizon through the earth’s daily rotation; it is not used when the sun or star is hidden by clouds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p319#2/r4.anchor: وهو المغيب الذي يكون بغروب الكوكب وراء الأفق بسبب الدورة اليومية للكرة الأرضية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p320/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p320/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p320/r1.claim: أحب here means approve or want: Ibrahim did not approve of, or want, a setting body as a deity, as established by هذا ربي; al-Zamakhshari instead supplies an omitted object, worship of those that set.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p320/r1.anchor: الحب فيه بمعنى الرضى والإرادة ، أي لا أرضى بالآفل إلها ، أو لا أريد الآفل إلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p320/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p320/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p320/r2.claim: The rational masculine plural الآفلين reflects Ibrahim’s people’s belief that stars are intelligent agents governing the universe, since a worshiped being must know.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p320/r2.anchor: بناء على اعتقاد قومه أن الكواكب عاقلة متصرفة في الأكوان ، ولا يكون الموجود معبودا إلا وهو عالم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p320/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p320/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p320/r3.claim: Setting disqualifies a star because a deity must continuously oversee servants, while the absent star cannot attend to their needs; Ibrahim argues from his people’s view that setting means absence from this world.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p320/r3.anchor: أن ما يغيب لا يستحق أن يتخذ إلها لأنه لا يغني عن عباده فيما يحتاجونه حين مغيبه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p320/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p320/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p320/r4.claim: The argument is not that change disproves divinity: his people did not accept that entailment, and setting is only an appearance to observers while the star remains in its orbit and returns.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p320/r4.anchor: ولأن الأفول ليس بتغير في ذات الكوكب بل هو عرض للأبصار المشاهدة له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p320/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p320/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p320/r5.claim: He argues from setting rather than rising because the earlier setting was not witnessed, making the point shorter than explaining that the rising star had previously set.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p320/r5.anchor: فكان الأفول أخصر في الاحتجاج من أن يقول : إن هذا البازغ كان من قبل آفلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r1.claim: The fa in falammā links the following clause and favors taking the ‘kingdom’ mentioned earlier as the detailed account that follows.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r1.anchor: هذه الفاء في قوله فلما رابطة جملة ما بعدها وهي ترجح أن المراد بالملكوت هو هذا التفصيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r2.claim: Janna al-layl means that night covered everything with darkness; jinn, majann, janna, and the grave called jannān likely derive from the root meaning ‘to cover.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r2.anchor: ويشبه أن يكون الجن والمجن والجنة والجنن وهو القبر مشتقة من جن إذا ستر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Abraham saw a star and worshipped it; many interpreters place the episode in his childhood before puberty and legal responsibility.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r3.anchor: كما ذهب إليه ابن عباس. فإنه قال: رأى كوكبا فعبده، وقاله ناس كثير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r4.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r4.claim: Another group places the episode after Abraham reached puberty and became accountable; al-Ṭabarī reports this position.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r4.anchor: وحكى الطبري هذا عن فرقة وقالت إنه استفهم على جهة التوقيف بغير ألف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r5.speaker: الشاعر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r5.claim: A poet’s line omits the interrogative hamza, supporting the claim that Abraham’s words could be a rebuking question without an expressed hamza.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r5.anchor: رقوني وقالوا يا خويلد لم ترع ... فقلت وأنكرت الوجوه هم هم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r6.speaker: الشاعر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r6.claim: A second poetic example likewise uses an omitted hamza in a question asking whether the named person is Shuʿayth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r6.anchor: لعمرك ما أدري وإن كنت داريا ... شعيث بن سهم أم شعيث بن منقر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the first poetic example provides no proof for omitting the interrogative hamza.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r8.claim: A tale says Nimrod’s astrologers predicted that a boy born in a certain year would overthrow him, so he had pregnant women watched and killed newborn boys.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r8.anchor: أن نمرود جبار ذلك الزمن رأى منجموه أن مولودا يولد في سنة كذا في عمله، يكون خراب الملك على يديه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r9.claim: In the tale, Abraham’s mother hid her pregnancy, gave birth in a cave while his father was away, and left him there.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r9.anchor: وأن أم إبراهيم حملت وكانت شابة قوية فسترت حملها فلما قربت ولادتها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r10.claim: The tale says Abraham lived by sucking his fingers, from which honey and butter came.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r10.anchor: وكانت تفتقده فتجده يغتذي بأن يمص أصابعه فيخرج له منها عسل وسمن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r11.claim: Other versions say an angel fed him, or that his mother brought milk from women whose sons had been killed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r11.anchor: وحكي بل كان يغذيه ملك وحكي بل كانت تأتيه بألبان النساء اللاتي ذبح أبناؤهن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r12.claim: The tale says Abraham grew unusually fast, remained hidden for ten or fifteen years, and saw the star when he first became aware of the world.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p312#2/r12.anchor: فشب إبراهيم أضعاف ما يشب غيره، والملك في خلال ذلك يحس بولادته ويشدد في طلبه فمكث في الغار عشرة أعوام وقيل خمس عشرة سنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the disagreement between ‘disappeared’ and ‘went away’ is verbal only.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r2.speaker: ذو الرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r2.claim: Dhū al-Rumma’s line uses āfilāt for the setting celestial lights, witnessing the word’s usage for bodies that disappear from view.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r2.anchor: مصابيح ليست باللواتي تقودها ... نجوم ولا بالآفلات الدوالك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r3.claim: The masculine sound plural āfilīn is used because the intended referents are lords; ‘this is my Lord’ points to the intended Lord.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r3.anchor: وقال الآفلين فجمع بالياء والنون لما قصد الأرباب ونحو ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r1.claim: جن عليه الليل means night darkened and covered him; جن and أجن are said of anything that covers, and the preferred expressions are جن عليه الليل and أجنه الليل.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r1.anchor: يقال جن عليه الليل وأجنه الليل إذا أظلم حتى يستر بظلمته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r2.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r2.claim: Ibrahim was born under Nimrod, whose soothsayers predicted a boy would destroy earthly idols, summon people to another religion, and bring his household's ruin; Nimrod ordered newborn boys killed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r2.anchor: روى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس قال ولد إبراهيم في زمن نمروذ وكان لنمروذ كهان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r3.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r3.claim: When labor began, Ibrahim's mother fled, hid him in a dry riverbed among reeds, and told Azar; his father dug a tunnel, sealed it with a stone, and his mother nursed him there.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r3.anchor: فلما أخذ أم إبراهيم المخاض خرجت هاربة فوضعته في نهر يابس ولفته في خرقة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r4.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r4.claim: As a child Ibrahim asked who his Lord was; his mother named herself, then his father, then his father's lord, before telling her husband the child would change the world's religion.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r4.anchor: وكانت أمه تختلف إليه فترضعه حتى شب وتكلم فقال لأمه من ربي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r5.speaker: ابن كثير وحفص عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r5.claim: For رأى in this verse, Ibn Kathir and Hafs read both the ra and hamza with fatḥa; Abu Amr has fatḥa on ra and kasra on hamza; Ibn Amir, Hamza, Kisai, and Abu Bakr have kasra on both.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r5.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وحفص عن عاصم رأى بفتح الراء والهمزة وقرأ أبو عمرو رإى بفتح الراء وكسر الهمزة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r6.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم وحمزة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r6.claim: The segment records additional variants for رأى when followed by a vowelless letter and when attached to a pronoun, naming the reciters and their ra and hamza treatments.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p72#2/r6.anchor: واختلفوا فيها إذا لقيها ساكن وهو آت في ستة مواضع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada identify the star Ibrahim saw as Venus.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r1.anchor: أحدهما أنه الزهرة قاله ابن عباس وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r2.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r2.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi identify the star as Jupiter.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r3.claim: A literal reading says Ibrahim worshipped the star, moon, and sun until each set, with the plea for guidance taken as evidence of uncertainty; the author rejects this, holding prophets protected from such error.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r3.anchor: روى علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال هذا ربي فعبده حتى غاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r4.claim: The literal-worship view is unacceptable because people prepared for prophethood are protected from this even in childhood.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r4.anchor: وهذا القول لا يرتضى والمتأهلون للنبوة محفوظون من مثل هذا على كل حال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r5.claim: The plea for guidance does not prove earlier doubt: prophets continually seek guidance and protection from error, as Abraham asked God to keep him and his children from idol worship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r5.anchor: فما زال الأنبياء يسألون الهدى ويتضرعون في دفع الضلال عنهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r6.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r6.claim: Another view treats this as a rhetorical step to expose the idols' failure at setting, with an implied “according to your claim” or “they say”; a reported wise man similarly led idolaters to pray to God, after which they converted.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r6.anchor: أنه قال ذلك استدراجا للحجة ليعيب آلهتهم ويريهم بغضها عند أفولها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r7.claim: A third view supplies a suppressed interrogative alif: “Is this my Lord?”; he calls this explanation anomalous because the interrogative particle distinguishes questions from statements and cannot be omitted.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r7.anchor: أنه قال مستفهما تقديره أهذا ربي فأضمرت ألف الاستفهام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r8.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r8.claim: The astrologers meant “this is what governs me”; Ibrahim argued that their supposed governor bears the signs of something governed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r8.anchor: كانوا أصحاب نجوم فقال هذا ربي أي هذا الذي يدبرني

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r9.claim: أفل means went out of sight or set; the verb is said يأفل and يأفل, with the verbal noun أفولا.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r9.anchor: وأفل بمعنى غاب يقال أفل النجم يأفل ويأفل أفولا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p75/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p75/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p75/r1.claim: Love of an eclipsing object is not the love owed to an object of worship, since what appears and sets is originated and governed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p75/r1.anchor: أي حب رب معبود لأن ما ظهر وأفل كان حادثا مدبرا

MAJAZ:v1p196/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p196/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p196/r8.claim: Janna ʿalayhi al-layl means the night covered him and became dark; the verbal noun is junūn.
MAJAZ:v1p196/r8.anchor:
«فلما جن عليه الليل» (76) أي: غطى عليه وأظلم عليه، ومصدره:
جن الليل جتونا،

MAJAZ:v1p196/r9.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p196/r9.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p196/r9.claim: Durayd ibn al-Ṣimma’s verse uses jann al-layl for the night’s covering darkness.
MAJAZ:v1p196/r9.anchor:
قال دريد بن الصمة:
ولولا جنون الليل أدرك ركضنا ... بذي الرمث والأرطي عياض بن ناشب

MAJAZ:v1p196/r10.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p196/r10.speaker: بعضهم
MAJAZ:v1p196/r10.claim: Some recite or transmit jinān al-layl, meaning its covering and blackness.
MAJAZ:v1p196/r10.anchor: وبعضهم ينشده: ولولا جنان الليل، أي غطاؤه وسواده،

MAJAZ:v1p196/r11.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p196/r11.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p196/r11.claim: Salāma ibn Jandal’s verse uses jinān for night’s covering, and Ibn Aḥmar’s line uses it for the Muslims’ darkness or blackness.
MAJAZ:v1p196/r11.anchor:
وقال سلامة بن جندل:
ولولا جنان الليل ما آب عامر ... إلى جعفر سرباله لم يمزق

MAJAZ:v1p196/r12.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p196/r12.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p196/r12.claim: Afala means disappeared or set; the imperfect has kasra on the fāʾ and the verbal noun is afūl, meaning disappearance.
MAJAZ:v1p196/r12.anchor: «فلما أفل» (76) أي غاب يقال: أين أفلت عنا، أي أين غبت عنا، وهو يأفل مكسورة الفاء،

MAJAZ:v1p196/r13.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p196/r13.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p196/r13.claim: A line about the Pleiades uses afūl for their disappearance; Dhū al-Rumma uses al-āfilāt for setting stars.
MAJAZ:v1p196/r13.anchor:
إذا ما الثريا أحست أفولا
أي: غيبوبة. [قال ذو الرمة:
مصابيح ليست باللواتي تقودها ... نجوم ولا بالآفلات الدوالك]

MAJAZ:v1p200/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p200/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p200/r1.claim: Al-āfilīn generalizes to all things that set, rather than naming only the sun, moon, and stars.
MAJAZ:v1p200/r1.anchor: «لا أحب الآفلين» (76) أي من الأشياء، ولم يقصد قصد الشمس والقمر والنجوم فيجمعها على جميع الموات.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r3.claim: “When night covered him” means night enveloped and concealed him; a kawkab is a star, and afala means it disappeared.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r3.anchor: وقوله: {فلما جن عليه الليل} أي: تغشاه وستره {رأى كوكبا} أي: نجما، {قال هذا ربي فلما أفل} أي: غاب.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r4.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق بن يسار
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq glosses afūl as going away; Ibn Jarir gives the verb's forms for a star's setting, and Dhu al-Rumma's line uses āfilāt for setting stars.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r4.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق بن يسار: "الأفول" الذهاب. وقال ابن جرير: يقال: أفل النجم يأفل ويأفل أفولا وأفلا إذا غاب، ومنه قول ذي الرمة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r5.claim: Qatada says Abraham knew that his Lord endures and does not disappear, unlike the celestial object.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r5.anchor: قال قتادة: علم أن ربه دائم لا يزول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r8.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r8.claim: Ibn Jarir understands Abraham's scene as contemplation and favors that reading because Abraham says that without his Lord's guidance he would be among the astray.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r8.anchor: فروى ابن جرير من طريق علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس ما يقتضي أنه مقام نظر، واختاره ابن جرير مستدلا بقوله: {لئن لم يهدني ربي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r9.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r9.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Abraham spoke after emerging from the cave where his mother had given birth and hidden him from Nimrod, who ordered boys killed after hearing of a child who would end his rule.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r9.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق: قال ذلك حين خرج من السرب الذي ولدته فيه أمه، حين تخوفت عليه النمرود بن كنعان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p292/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p292/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p292/r3.claim: The planets' fixed, God-governed paths and lack of self-direction disqualify them from divinity; Abraham demonstrates this successively for Venus, the moon, and the sun.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p292/r3.anchor: لأنها مسخرة مقدرة بسير معين، لا تزيغ عنه يمينا ولا شمالا ولا تملك لنفسها تصرفا، بل هي جرم من الأجرام خلقها الله منيرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p292#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p292#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p292#2/r1.claim: The Prophet reports that every newborn is born upon the fitra, supporting Ibn Kathir's rejection of the idea that Abraham was still searching for true belief.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p292#2/r1.anchor: وقد ثبت في الصحيحين، عن أبي هريرة، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "كل مولود يولد على الفطرة" (1)

JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو وورش عن نافع
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Warsh from Nāfiʿ open the rāʾ and kasra the hamza after the alif in raʾā throughout.
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وورش عن نافع: رأى بفتح الراء وكسر الهمزة بعد الألف حيث كان

JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r2.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī generally kasra both rāʾ and hamza, with differences before k or h and before a connecting alif.
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي بكسرهما

JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r3.speaker: يحيى عن أبي بكر عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r3.claim: Yaḥyā from Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim transmits the same reading as Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī in the specified environment.
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r3.anchor: وروى يحيى عن أبي بكر عن عاصم مثل قراءة حمزة والكسائي

JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r4.speaker: حمزة ويحيى عن أبي بكر ونصيرا عن الكسائي
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r4.claim: When raʾā is followed by an alif of connection, these readers kasra the rāʾ and open the hamza.
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r4.anchor: فإن حمزة ويحيى عن أبي بكر ونصيرا عن الكسائي يكسرون الراء ويفتحون الهمزة

JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r5.claim: The other readers open both vowels; all agree on the fatḥa in raʾūka and raʾathum, and imāla follows the yāʾ which drops before a connecting alif.
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ الباقون جميع ذلك بفتح الراء والهمزة، واتفقوا في رأوك ورأتهم بالفتح

JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r6.claim: Janna means to cover; the root also explains the words for garden, jinn, madness, fetus, shield, and heart as concealed or concealing.
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r6.anchor: جن: ستر، وأصل الباب: الستر، ومنه: الجنة؛ لأن الشجر سترها، والجن لاستتارهم عن العيون

JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r7.claim: Janna ʿalayhi al-layl means the night darkened over him; jannahu means covered him without the added sense of darkness.
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r7.anchor: وجن عليه: الليل أظلم عليه، وجنه: ستره من غير تضمين بمعنى أظلم

JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r8.claim: The form janna ʿalayhi without an alif is more eloquent and is the Qurʾānic wording.
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r8.anchor: وطرح الألف من عليه أفصح، وبذلك ورد القرآن

JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r9.claim: Afūl means setting or disappearing; afalat can be pronounced with either kasra or ḍamma on the fāʾ.
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r9.anchor: والأفول: الغروب، أفل يأفل أفولا، وأفل: إذا غاب

JISHUMI:v3p2296/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2296/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2296/r8.claim: The passage follows God's signs shown to Abraham and explains his reasoning and recognition of truth.
JISHUMI:v3p2296/r8.anchor: لما تقدم ذكر الآيات التي أراها الله تعالى إبراهيم بين كيف استدل، وكيف اعترف بالحق، فقال سبحانه

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p133/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p133/r15.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p133/r15.claim: Mujahid says the star Abraham saw was Venus, which rose at dusk.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p133/r15.anchor: قال مجاهد : ذكر لنا أنه رأى الزهرة طلعت عشاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p133/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p133/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p133/r16.claim: The night covering Abraham is glossed as covering or concealing him; related words for garden, jinn, madness, fetus, and shield likewise evoke concealment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p133/r16.anchor: ومعنى جن عليه الليل , أي ستره , ولذلك سمي البستان جنة لأن الشجر يسترها , والجن لاستتارهم عن العيون

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r1.claim: The Hudhayli poetic line uses جنه for something covered by the dark dusk.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r1.anchor: وماء وردت قيل الكرى … وقد جنه السدف الأدهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r2.claim: One interpretation is that Abraham said this as a provisional supposition while reasoning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r2.anchor: أنه قال : هذا ربي في ظني , لأنه في حال تقليب واستدلال

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abraham actually believed the star was his Lord.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r3.anchor: أنه قال ذلك اعتقادا أنه ربه , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r4.claim: Another view places the statement in Abraham's childhood, before proof and before a state in which belief or unbelief applied.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r4.anchor: أنه قال ذلك في حال الطفولية والصغر , لأن أمه ولدته في مغارة حذرا عليه من نمرود

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r5.claim: Another view says he did not speak in belief but rejected idol worship: even greater heavenly bodies cannot be gods if they set, so handmade idols are less worthy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r5.anchor: لم يقل ذلك قول معتقد , وإنما قاله على وجه الإنكار لعبادة الأصنام , فإذا كان الكوكب والشمس القمر وما لم تصنعه يد

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r6.claim: A further view reads this as a rebuke in the form of a rhetorical question: Is this my Lord?
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r6.anchor: أنه قال ذلك توبيخا على وجه الإنكار الذي يكون معه ألف الاستفهام وتقديره : أهذا ربي , كما قال الشاعر

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r7.claim: Setting means disappearing; Dhu al-Rumma's line uses الآفلات for stars that set.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p136/r7.anchor: أي غاب , قال ذو الرمة : مصابيح ليست باللواتي يقودها

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137/r1.claim: Not loving the setting stars means not loving them as a worshipped Lord; ordinary affection for them is unobjectionable.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137/r1.anchor: يعني حب رب معبود , وإلا فلا حرج في محبتهم غير حب الرب

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137/r3.claim: Setting proves celestial bodies cannot be worshipped because their change shows they are governed and originated, and what has that quality cannot be a deity.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137/r3.anchor: لأن تغيرها بالأفول دليل على أنها مدبرة محدثة , وما كان بهذه الصفة استحال أن يكون إلها معبودا

MUJAHID:v1p218#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p218#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p218#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قال ﴿ ملكوت ﴾ الآيات

NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r1.claim: جنّ الليل means the night became dark; the clause is coordinated with Abraham's earlier statement to his father, while “Thus We showed Abraham” is parenthetical.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r1.anchor: أى أظلم وهو عطف على قال إبراهيم لأبيه وقوله وكذلك نرى إبراهيم جملة اعتراضية

NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r2.claim: The star Abraham saw was either Venus or Jupiter.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r2.anchor: ﴿ رأى كوكبا ﴾ أى الزهرة أو المشترى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r3.claim: Because Abraham's people worshipped idols, sun, moon, and stars, he meant to expose their error and lead them to reason that these originated, changing bodies have a maker who directs their rising, setting, movement, and other states.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r3.anchor: فأراد أن ينبههم على الخطأ فى دينهم و أن يرشدهم إلى طريق النظر والاستدلال

NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r4.claim: “This is my lord” can mean “this is your lord, as you claim,” or be a mocking rhetorical question; Arabs can signal a question by vocal tone without an interrogative particle.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r4.anchor: أى قال لهم هذا ربى فى زعمكم أو المراد أهذا استهزاء بهم وانكارا عليهم والعرب تكتفى عن حرف الاستفهام بنغمة الصوت

NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r5.claim: The author prefers Abraham's fair-minded rehearsal of an opponent's claim: it is less partisan, better leads to truth and avoids dispute, before he refutes it with proof.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r5.anchor: والصحيح أن هذا قول من ينصف خصمه مع علمه أنه مبطل فيحكى قوله كما هو

NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r6.claim: أفل means the star disappeared; Abraham rejects worship of gods that change from one state to another, since change characterizes bodies.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#2/r6.anchor: أى لا أحب عبادة الأرباب المتغيرين عن حال إلى حال لأن ذلك من صفات الأجسام

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r1.claim: Janna and related words share the sense of covering: the garden, fetus, shield, and jinn are all named in connection with concealment.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r1.anchor: ومنه الجنة والجنة والجنة والجنين والمجن والجن كله بمعنى الستر.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r2.claim: Jinān al-layl is the darkness and concealment of night; the same phrase appears in a line by a poet.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r2.anchor:
وجنان الليل ادلهمامه وستره. قال الشاعر:
ولولا جنان الليل أدرك ركضنا
بذي الرمث والأرطى عياض بن ناشب

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r3.claim: Another expression is junūn al-layl, and both jannah al-layl and ajannah al-layl are used for night covering someone.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r3.anchor: ويقال: جنون الليل أيضا. ويقال: جنه الليل وأجنه الليل، لغتان.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r4.claim: This is a different story from God's showing Abraham the dominion of the heavens and earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r4.anchor: هذه قصة أخرى، غير قصة عرض الملكوت عليه.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r5.claim: One account says Abraham saw the star through a split in the rock covering the cave entrance.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r5.anchor: فقيل: رأى ذلك من شق الصخرة الموضوعة على رأس السرب.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r6.claim: Another account says that after his father took him from the cave at sunset, he saw livestock and reasoned that they must have a Lord.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r6.anchor: وقيل: لما أخرجه أبوه من السرب وكان وقت غيبوبة الشمس فرأى الإبل والخيل والغنم فقال: لا بد لها من رب.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r7.claim: One account has him see Jupiter or Venus, then the moon, then the sun, at the end of the month.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r7.anchor: ورأى المشتري أو الزهرة ثم القمر ثم الشمس، وكان هذا في آخر الشهر.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r8.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r8.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Abraham was fifteen years old.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r8.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق: وكان ابن خمس عشرة سنة.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r9.claim: Another report says he was seven years old.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r10.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r10.claim: A further account says he was seventeen when he argued with Nimrod.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r10.anchor: وقيل: لما حاج نمروذا كان ابن سبع عشرة سنة.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r11.claim: One view places Abraham's statement during childhood and before the proof was established, a period in which there is neither disbelief nor faith.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r11.anchor: فقيل: كان هذا منه في مهلة النظر وحال الطفولية وقبل قيام الحجة وفي تلك الحال لا يكون كفر ولا إيمان.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r12.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r12.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says Abraham worshipped the star, moon, and sun until they set, then declared himself free of what his people associated; proponents cite setting as the clearest sign of createdness.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r12.anchor: فاستدل قائلو هذه المقالة بما روي عن علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال: «فلما جن عليه الليل رأى كوكبا قال هذا ربي» فعبده حتى غاب عنه،

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r13.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r13.claim: Another group says a prophet cannot pass through any period without knowing and affirming God and rejecting every other object of worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r13.anchor: وقال قوم: هذا لا يصح وقالوا: غير جائز أن يكون لله تعالى رسول

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r14.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r14.claim: They argue that Abraham was protected, shown God's dominion to become certain, and could not have lacked knowledge; he knew the Lord from his first reflection.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r14.anchor: وأراه ملكوته ليكون من الموقنين، ولا يجوز أن يوصف بالخلو عن المعرفة، بل عرف الرب أول النظر.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r15.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r15.claim: Al-Zajjāj calls the childhood explanation mistaken and cites Abraham's prayer not to worship idols and the description of his sound heart as evidence that he never associated partners.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r15.anchor:
قال الزجاج: هذا الجواب عندي خطأ وغلط ممن قاله وقد أخبر الله تعالى عن إبراهيم أنه قال:
واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r16.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r16.claim: Al-Zajjāj's explanation is that Abraham said 'this is my Lord' in the sense of speaking according to his people's belief, like the divine phrase 'Where are My partners?'
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r16.anchor: والجواب عندي أنه قال: { هذا ربي } على قولكم لأنهم كانوا يعبدون الأصنام والشمس والقمر ونظير هذا قوله تعالى: «أين شركائي»

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r17.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r17.claim: Another view says Abraham left the cave seeking his Lord and mistook the star's light for the Lord's light; when it set, he knew it was not his Lord.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r17.anchor: وقيل: لما خرج إبراهيم من السرب رأى ضوء الكوكب وهو طالب لربه فظن أنه ضوءه قال: { هذا ربي }

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r18.claim: The account does not imply that Abraham committed shirk.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76/r18.anchor: فلما أفل قال لئن لم يهدني ربي لأكونن من القوم الضالين. فلما رأى الشمس بازغة قال هذا ربي } وليس هذا شركا.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r1.claim: When the light disappeared, Abraham knew it did not deserve lordship, rejected it inwardly, and knew it was created rather than creator.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r1.anchor: فلما رآه زائلا دله العلم على أنه غير مستحق لذلك فنفاه بقلبه وعلم أنه مربوب وليس برب.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r2.claim: Another view says Abraham pretended to agree with his people in order to establish the argument: once the star set, he showed that what changes cannot be Lord; they revered, worshipped, and judged by stars.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: إنما قال { هذا ربي } لتقرير الحجة على قومه فأظهر موافقتهم فلما أفل النجم قرر الحجة وقال: ما تغير لا يجوز أن يكون ربا.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r3.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r3.claim: Al-Naḥḥās calls the report from Ibn ʿAbbās on 'light upon light' one of the best explanations: the believer knows God by the heart and reasons from signs, as Abraham did, then receives increased knowledge when God makes Himself known.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r3.anchor:
وقال النحاس: ومن أحسن ما قيل في هذا ما صح عن ابن عباس أنه قال في قول الله عز وجل:
نور على نور

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r4.claim: One interpretation reads the words as a question and rebuke: 'Is this my Lord?' or 'Can something like this be a lord?', with the interrogative hamza omitted.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو على معنى الاستفهام والتوبيخ، منكرا لفعلهم. والمعنى أهذا ربي، أو مثل هذا يكون ربا؟ فحذف الهمزة.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r5.claim: The Qurʾānic example 'If I die, are they immortal?' likewise omits an interrogative hamza.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r5.anchor:
وفي التنزيل
أفإن مت فهم الخالدون
[الأنبياء: 34] أي أفهم الخالدون.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r6.speaker: الهذلي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r6.claim: A Huthali poet's lines illustrate omission of the interrogative hamza, including the expression 'they are they'.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r6.anchor:
وقال الهذلي:
رفوني وقالوا يا خويلد لا ترع
فقلت وأنكرت الوجوه هم هم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r7.speaker: الهذلي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r7.claim: A second Huthali poetic example likewise leaves the interrogative unexpressed in asking whether the stones were seven or eight.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r7.anchor:
آخر:
لعمرك ما أدري وإن كنت داريا
بسبع رمين الجمر أم بثمان

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r8.claim: Another interpretation takes Abraham to mean that this was his Lord according to the claim of his people, like the verse about alleged divine partners.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r8.anchor:
وقيل: المعنى هذا ربي على زعمكم كما قال تعالى:
أين شركآئي الذين كنتم تزعمون
[القصص: 62].

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r9.claim: Another view supplies an omitted 'you say': that is, 'you say this is my Lord'; omission of such words is common in the Qurʾān.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: المعنى أي وأنتم تقولون هذا ربي فأضمر القول، وإضماره في القرآن كثير.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r10.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r10.claim: A further view takes the star or luminary as evidence pointing to Abraham's Lord.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: المعنى في هذا ربي أي هذا دليل على ربي.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r11.claim: The phrase 'You are indeed the mighty and noble' is glossed as describing how the addressee sees himself.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:76#2/r11.anchor:
وقال:
ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم
[الدخان: 49] أي عند نفسك.

RAZI-FULL:v13p29/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p29/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p29/r1.claim: Abraham's debate is an argument against Arab polytheists because all religious communities honored him, and the polytheists acknowledged both his merit and their descent from him.
RAZI-FULL:v13p29/r1.anchor: المشركون كانوا معترفين بفضله مقرين بأنهم من أولاده واليهود والنصارى والمسلمون كلهم معظمون له

RAZI-FULL:v13p29/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p29/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p29/r2.claim: Abraham's unique standing followed a covenant: he fulfilled servanthood, as God attests both generally and specifically in the trials and command to submit.
RAZI-FULL:v13p29/r2.anchor: فإبراهيم وفى بعهد العبودية ، والله تعالى شهد بذلك على سبيل الإجمال تارة وعلى سبيل التفصيل أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v13p29/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p29/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p29/r3.claim: Abraham demonstrated monotheism in debates with his father, his people, and the ruler, by smashing idols, enduring the threat of burning, and offering his son.
RAZI-FULL:v13p29/r3.anchor: ناظر في إثبات التوحيد وإبطال القول بالشركاء والأنداد في مقامات كثيرة

RAZI-FULL:v13p29/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p29/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p29/r4.claim: He gave his heart to knowledge, tongue to proof, body to fire, child to sacrifice, and wealth to guests; God answered his prayer for lasting good mention, making him honored among all communities.
RAZI-FULL:v13p29/r4.anchor: سلم قلبه للعرفان ولسانه للبرهان وبدنه للنيران وولده للقربان وماله للضيفان

RAZI-FULL:v13p29/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p29/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p29/r5.claim: Because Arabs acknowledged Abraham's merit, God made his debate with his people a proof against Arab polytheists.
RAZI-FULL:v13p29/r5.anchor: ولما كان العرب معترفين بفضله لا جرم جعل الله تعالى مناظرته مع قومه حجة على مشركي العرب

RAZI-FULL:v13p39/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p39/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v13p39/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the clause about night covering Abraham coordinates with Abraham's speech to his father, while “Thus We showed” is an intervening parenthesis.
RAZI-FULL:v13p39/r1.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : { فلما جن عليه اليل } عطف على قوله : { قال إبراهيم لابيه ءازر }

RAZI-FULL:v13p39/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p39/r2.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v13p39/r2.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says the preferred idioms are “night covered him” and “night came over him”; janna means concealment and underlies the listed words for garden, jinn, madness, embryo, and grave.
RAZI-FULL:v13p39/r2.anchor: هذا قول جميع أهل اللغة ، ومعنى { جن } ستر ومنه الجنة والجن والجنون

RAZI-FULL:v13p39/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p39/r3.speaker: بعض النحويين
RAZI-FULL:v13p39/r3.claim: Some grammarians take janna ʿalayhi al-layl to mean that night darkened over him, which accounts for ʿalā; jannahū means simply covered him without the sense of darkness.
RAZI-FULL:v13p39/r3.anchor: وقال بعض النحويين : { جن عليه اليل } إذا أظلم عليه الليل

RAZI-FULL:v13p39/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p39/r4.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v13p39/r4.claim: Most exegetes recount that a king, warned a boy would contest his rule, ordered newborn boys killed; Abraham was hidden in a cave, miraculously sustained by Gabriel, and later sought his Lord after his mother and father answered that they served as his lords and the king ruled them.
RAZI-FULL:v13p39/r4.anchor: فأمر ذلك الملك بذبح كل غلام يولد ، فحبلت أم إبراهيم به وماأظهرت حبلها للناس

RAZI-FULL:v13p39/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p39/r5.speaker: أكثر المحققين
RAZI-FULL:v13p39/r5.claim: Most rigorous scholars reject the view that Abraham's stargazing occurred after puberty and the onset of legal responsibility; they argue against it in the following discussion.
RAZI-FULL:v13p39/r5.anchor: واتفق أكثر المحققين على فساد القول الأول واحتجوا عليه بوجوه

RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r1.claim: Argument one: affirming a star as Lord is unanimously disbelief, and disbelief is unanimously impossible for prophets.
RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r1.anchor: أن القول بربوبية النجم كفر بالإجماع والكفر غير جائز بالإجماع على الأنبياء

RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r2.claim: Argument two: Abraham already knew his Lord, since he had confronted his father Āzar about taking idols as gods before this episode.
RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r2.anchor: أنه تعالى أخبر عنه أنه قال قبل هذه الواقعة لأبيه آزر

RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r3.claim: Argument three: Abraham first used gentle speech with his father; a preacher resorts to harshness only after sustained gentle appeals and despair, so the episode came after he knew God and had repeatedly called his father.
RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r3.anchor: من دعا غيره إلى الله تعالى فإنه يقدم الرفق على العنف واللين على الغلظ

RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r4.claim: Argument four: after God showed Abraham the kingdom of heaven and earth, it is inconceivable that he would regard celestial bodies as divine.
RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r4.anchor: ومن كان منصبه في الدين كذلك ، وعلمه بالله كذلك ، كيف يليق به أن يعتقد إلهية الكواكب ؟

RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r5.claim: Argument five: the heavens display at least fifteen signs of origination, making star-worship implausible even for a person of little reason, let alone Abraham.
RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r5.anchor: دلائل الحدوث في الأفلاك ظاهرة من خمسة عشر وجها وأكثر

RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p39#2/r6.claim: Argument six: God calls Abraham pure of heart, which at minimum means free from disbelief, and says he received sound guidance from early in his reflection; God knows where to place His message.

RAZI-FULL:v13p40/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p40/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p40/r1.claim: Argument seven: the narrative's sequence places the stargazing after God showed Abraham the kingdom of the heavens and earth and made him certain in faith.
RAZI-FULL:v13p40/r1.anchor: والفاء تقتضي الترتيب ، فثبت أن هذه الواقعة إنما وقعت بعد أن صار إبراهيم من الموقنين العارفين بربه

RAZI-FULL:v13p40/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p40/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p40/r2.claim: Argument eight: the passage identifies the debate as proof against Abraham's people, showing that he argued to guide them rather than seek knowledge for himself.
RAZI-FULL:v13p40/r2.anchor: ولم يقل على نفسه ، فعلم أن هذه المباحثة إنما جرت مع قومه لأجل أن يرشدهم إلى الإيمان والتوحيد

RAZI-FULL:v13p40#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p40#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p40#2/r3.claim: First explanation, which Razi calls the relied-upon answer: Abraham repeats the star-worshippers' claim so he can refute it, just as a debater restates an opponent's premise before exposing its contradiction.
RAZI-FULL:v13p40#2/r3.anchor: بل الغرض منه أنه كان يناظر عبدة الكوكب وكان مذهبهم أن الكوكب ربهم وآلههم

RAZI-FULL:v13p41/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p41/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p41/r2.claim: A third explanation treats the words as a rhetorical question of denial, with the interrogative particle omitted because the context makes it clear.
RAZI-FULL:v13p41/r2.anchor: المراد منه الاستفهام على سبيل الإنكار إلا أنه أسقط

RAZI-FULL:v13p41/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p41/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p41/r3.claim: A fourth explanation supplies an omitted “they say”: Abraham tells his people that they claim this is the one who manages and raises him, as in other verses with implicit speech.

RAZI-FULL:v13p41/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p41/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p41/r4.claim: A fifth explanation reads the statement as mockery, like sarcastically calling a lowly person who has become leader “your master.”
RAZI-FULL:v13p41/r4.anchor: أن يكون إبراهيم ذكر هذا الكلام على سبيل الاستهزاء

RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r1.claim: The account that Abraham was born in a cave, left there by his mother, and raised by Gabriel is generally possible.
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r1.anchor: إبراهيم عليه السلام ولد في الغار وتركته أمه وكان جبريل عليه السلام يربيه كل ذلك محتمل في الجملة

RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r2.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r2.claim: The Qadi rejects irhāṣ, miracles before a prophetic mission, unless a messenger is present so the marvel can count as that prophet’s miracle.
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r2.anchor: كل ما يجري مجرى المعجزات فإنه لا يجوز لأن تقديم المعجز على وقت الدعوى غير جائز عندهم

RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r3.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r3.claim: The author’s school permits irhāṣ, removing the objection to the cave story.
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r3.anchor: وأما عند أصحابنا فالإرهاص جائز فزالت الشبهة والله أعلم

RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r4.claim: Afūl means a thing’s disappearance after it has appeared.
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r4.anchor: الأفول عبارة عن غيبوبة الشيء بعد ظهوره

RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r5.claim: Although rising and setting both indicate origination through motion, setting is clearer to ordinary hearers; motion’s proof is subtle and understood only by the elite.
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r5.anchor: دلالة الحركة على الحدوث وإن كانت يقينية إلا أنها دقيقة لا يعرفها إلا الأفاضل من الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r6.speaker: بعض المحققين
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r6.claim: The elite read setting as contingency: every possible thing needs a cause, and dependence must end at one beyond possibility, as 53:42 says.
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r6.anchor: قال بعض المحققين : الهوى في خطرة الإمكان أفول

RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r7.speaker: الأوساط
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r7.claim: Middle hearers read setting as motion: every moving thing is originated and depends on the eternal, capable creator.
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r7.anchor: وأما الأوساط فإنهم يفهمون من الأفول مطلق الحركة

RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r8.speaker: العوام
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r8.claim: Ordinary people see a setting star lose light, strength, and rule; something so diminished cannot be divine.
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r8.anchor: كل كوكب يقرب من الأفول والغروب فإنه يزول نوره وينتقص ضوءه ويذهب سلطانه

RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r9.claim: The single phrase reaches the elite, middling hearers, and common people, making it a complete and excellent proof.
RAZI-FULL:v13p43/r9.anchor: كلمة مشتملة على نصيب المقربين وأصحاب اليمين وأصحاب الشمال

RAZI-FULL:v13p43#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p43#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p43#2/r1.claim: Abraham addresses astrologers: by their doctrine, a star is powerful while rising in the east but weak and ineffectual near setting, exposing its inability to govern.
RAZI-FULL:v13p43#2/r1.anchor: في الربع الغربي ، يكون ضعيف القوة ، ناقص التأثير ، عاجزا عن التدبير

RAZI-FULL:v13p43#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p43#2/r2.speaker: المنجمون وأصحاب الوسايط
RAZI-FULL:v13p43#2/r2.claim: They allow created planets to remain subordinate lords: the supreme deity creates them, then they create plants and animals in the lower world.
RAZI-FULL:v13p43#2/r2.anchor: أن الإله الأكبر خلق الكواكب وأبدعها وأحدثها ، ثم أن هذه الكواكب تخلق النبات والحيوان في هذا العالم الأسفل

RAZI-FULL:v13p43#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p43#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p43#2/r3.claim: If Lord means the final terminus of need, an originated star cannot be Lord because every originated thing depends on another for existence.
RAZI-FULL:v13p43#2/r3.anchor: أن يكون المراد من الرب والإله الموجود الذي عنده تنقطع الحاجات

RAZI-FULL:v13p43#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p43#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p43#2/r4.claim: If Lord means the one who creates us and gives our essences and attributes existence, a setting star is also disqualified.
RAZI-FULL:v13p43#2/r4.anchor: من يكون خالقا لنا وموجدا لذواتنا وصفاتنا

RAZI-FULL:v13p43#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p43#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p43#2/r5.claim: A star’s origination entails dependence on an eternal agent whose power must itself be eternal, or an infinite regress of agents follows.
RAZI-FULL:v13p43#2/r5.anchor: وإلا لافتقرت قادريته إلى قادر آخر ، ولزم التسلسل وهو محال

RAZI-FULL:v13p44/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p44/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p44/r1.claim: Possibility is common to every possible thing; whatever makes one possible thing subject to God’s power therefore makes all such things subject to Him.
RAZI-FULL:v13p44/r1.anchor: والإمكان واحد في كل الممكنات . فثبت أن ما لأجله صار بعض الممكنات مقدورا لله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v13p44/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p44/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p44/r2.claim: The Qur’an states only the foundational premises; the detailed demonstration belongs to dialectic, while setting signals that celestial bodies cannot create or originate.
RAZI-FULL:v13p44/r2.anchor: ودلائل القرآن إنما يذكر فيها أصول المقدمات ، فأما التفريع والتفصيل ، فذاك إنما يليق بعلم الجدل

RAZI-FULL:v13p44/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p44/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p44/r3.claim: Because setting shows the stars and spheres depend on a creator, that creator’s ability to make the greater entails ability to create humans; 40:57 and 36:81 support the comparison.
RAZI-FULL:v13p44/r3.anchor: ومن كان قادرا على خلق الكواكب والأفلاك من دون واسطة أي شيء كان فبأن يكون قادرا على خلق الإنسان أولى

RAZI-FULL:v13p44/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p44/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p44/r4.claim: The supreme creator can create and govern the lower world without celestial intermediaries, so worship of Him takes priority over worship of sun, stars, or moon.
RAZI-FULL:v13p44/r4.anchor: كان الاشتغال بعبادة الإله الأكبر أولى من الاشتغال بعبادة الشمس والنجوم والقمر

RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r1.claim: If any star were a creator, people could not know which star or combination made them; assigning creation to the creator of all makes knowing, worshipping, and thanking Him possible.
RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r1.anchor: فثبت بهذه الوجوه أن أفول الكواكب كما يدل على امتناع كونها قديمة فكذلك يدل على امتناع كونها آلهة لهذا العالم

RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r2.speaker: سائل
RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r2.claim: An objector asks what special force this night’s setting adds, since the stars, moon, and sun had already set on earlier nights and days.
RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r2.anchor: كان أفول الكواكب والقمر والشمس حاصلا في الليل السابق والنهار السابق

RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r3.claim: Abraham could have debated star worshippers on a particular night and pointed out, as each body set in turn, its loss of strength and rule.
RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r3.anchor: كان جالسا مع أولئك الأقوام ليلة من الليالي وزجرهم عن عبادة الكواكب

RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r4.speaker: الغزالي
RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r4.claim: Ghazali assigns the star to its animal rational soul, the moon to the rational soul of its sphere, and the sun to the separate intellect.
RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r4.anchor: حمل الكوكب على النفس الناطقة الحيوانية التي لكل كوكب ، والقمر على النفس الناطقة التي لكل فلك ، والشمس على العقل المجرد الذي لكل ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r5.speaker: أبو علي بن سيناء
RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r5.claim: Ibn Sina interprets setting as possibility; Ghazali takes the things’ possibility in themselves to imply a cause culminating in the Necessary Existent.
RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r5.anchor: وكان أبو علي بن سيناء يفسر الأفول بالإمكان

RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r6.speaker: الغزالي
RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r6.claim: Ghazali reads the phrase as saying that all these things are possible in themselves, so each needs an efficient cause and ultimately a Necessary Existent.
RAZI-FULL:v13p45/r6.anchor: كل ممكن فلا بد له من مؤثر ، ولا بد له من الانتهاء إلى واجب الوجود

RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r1.claim: The author finds Ghazali’s interpretation acceptable in itself but unlikely to fit the verse’s wording.
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r1.anchor: هذا الكلام لا بأس به . إلا أنه يبعد حمل لفظ الآية عليه

RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r2.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r2.claim: Some map star, moon, and sun to sense, imagination and estimation, and intellect; these finite faculties are ruled by the governor of the world.
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r2.anchor: ومن الناس من حمل الكوكب على الحس والقمر على الخيال والوهم ، والشمس على العقل

RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r3.claim: God is not a body: a body would always be absent from us and thus always setting; divine descent and ascent would likewise imply setting.
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r3.anchor: هذه الآية تدل على أنه تعالى ليس بجسم إذ لو كان جسما لكان غائبا عنا أبدا

RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r4.claim: God cannot be a locus for originated attributes, as the Karrāmiyya say, because change would entail the impossible condition of setting.
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r4.anchor: هذه الآية تدل على أنه تعالى ليس محلا للصفات المحدثة كما تقوله الكرامية ، وإلا لكان متغيرا

RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r5.claim: Religion must rest on evidence rather than imitation, or Abraham’s argument would have no purpose.
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r5.anchor: أن الدين يجب أن يكون مبنيا على الدليل لا على التقليد

RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r6.claim: The verse indicates that prophets’ knowledge of their Lord is inferential rather than necessary or innate.
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r6.anchor: أن معارف الأنبياء بربهم استدلالية لا ضرورية

RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r7.claim: Knowledge of God is attained only by examining and reasoning from the conditions of His creatures.
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r7.anchor: أنه لا طريق إلى تحصيل معرفة الله تعالى إلا بالنظر والاستدلال في أحوال مخلوقاته

SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r1.claim: فلما جن may coordinate with وإذ قال إبراهيم, with وكذلك نري إبراهيم parenthetical, or with the sentence كذلك نري إبراهيم; the author prefers the first, as does al-Zamakhsharī.

SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the فاء links the episode to what precedes and favors reading the kingdom’s unveiling as the detailed account in these verses.
SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطية: " الفاء في قوله: " فلما " رابطة جملة ما بعدها بما قبلها،

SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r3.claim: جن means to cover; with night, جن عليه الليل and أجنه الليل mean it became dark, while جنه and أجنه can also be transitive, though the best usage makes the three-letter form intransitive and the derived form transitive.
SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r3.anchor: يقال: جن عليه الليل وأجن عليه، بمعنى أظلم، فيستعمل قاصرا، وجنه وأجنه فيستعمل متعديا

SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r4.claim: The verse’s جن may be transitive with its object omitted, understood as the things and visible objects covered by night.
SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون " جن " في الآية الكريمة متعديا حذف المفعول منه تقديره: جن عليه الأشياء والمبصرات.

SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r5.claim: A poetic citation attests the less usual transitive use of جن, describing dark nightfall covering water.
SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r5.anchor: وماء وردت قبيل الكرى وقد جنه السدف الأدهم

SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r6.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r6.claim: Al-Rāghib distinguishes جنه, to cover it, from أجنه, to provide it with something that covers it, comparing قبرته وأقبرته and سقيته وأسقيته.
SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r6.anchor: فرق الراغب بين جنه وأجنه، فقال: " جنه إذا ستره، وأجنه جعل له

SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r7.claim: For رأى written with its alif, several readers apply full or partial imāla: the two readers, Abū Bakr, Ibn Dhakwān, Abū ʿAmr, al-Sūsī in one route, and Warsh between the vowels, with the stated conditions.
SAMIN-DURR:6:76/r7.anchor: فأمال راءه وهمزته إمالة محضة الأخوان وأبو بكر عن عاصم وابن ذكوان عن ابن عامر،

SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r1.claim: The cited line هنادك appears to support an extra initial kāf in هندكي, but grammarians analyze it as a longer paired form like سبط and سبطر, not as an added root letter.
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r1.anchor: فظاهره زيادة الكاف، ولكن خرجها النحويون على أنه من باب سبط وسبطر

SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r2.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r2.claim: The Shaykh questions which expert grammarians allow an extra kāf, especially at a word’s beginning.
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r2.anchor: قال الشيخ، " وليت شعري: من حذاق النحويين الذين يرون زيادتها لا سيما أول الكلمة "

SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r3.claim: A second etymology treats the whole word as a rare quadriliteral with a repeated first radical, on the pattern فعفل, like فوفل.
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r3.anchor: والثاني: أن الكلمة كلها أصول رباعية، مما كررت فيها الفاء فوزنها فعفل ك " فوفل "

SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r4.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r4.claim: Al-Rāghib derives كوكب from كب and كبكب, suggesting an extra wāw and a kāf substituted for one yāʾ; the author calls this very strange.
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r4.anchor: الثالث: ساق الراغب أنه من مادة: كب وكبكب

SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r5.claim: قال هذا ربي is most plausibly an independent statement, whether reported declaratively or as a question; two less persuasive parses make it an adjective of كوكبا or the answer to فلما.
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r5.anchor: في " قال " ثلاثة أوجه، أظهرها: أنه استئناف أخبر بذلك القول أو استفهم عنه

SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r6.claim: He rejects taking قال as an adjective of كوكبا because there is no suitable linking pronoun and the sense would wrongly describe the star as uttering the statement.
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r6.anchor: أما الصناعة فلعدم الضمير العائد من الجملة الواقعة صفة إلى موصوفها، ولا يقال: إن الرابط حصل باسم الإشارة

SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r7.claim: If قال answers فلما, رأى كوكبا becomes a circumstantial clause describing Abraham as seeing the star.
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#2/r7.anchor: والثالث: أنه جواب " فلما جن، وعلى هذا فيكون قوله " رأى كوكبا " في محل نصب على الحال

SAMIN-DURR:6:76#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#3/r1.claim: The poetry and Qurʾanic examples supply omitted interrogative hamza before predicate phrases, illustrating the question reading of this passage.
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#3/r1.anchor: قالوا: تقديره: أبسبع، وأأفرح، وأذو، وأتلك.

SAMIN-DURR:6:76#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#3/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#3/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says an omitted interrogative hamza is permissible only when a verbal clue, such as أم, separates the predicate from the question.
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: " وهذا لا يجوز إلا حيث يكون ثم فاصل بين الخبر والاستفهام،

SAMIN-DURR:6:76#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#3/r3.claim: The cited poetry and Qurʾanic construction are offered as examples of omitted interrogative hamza; Ibn al-Anbārī accepts only the example with the explicit separator أم.
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#3/r3.anchor: يعني إن دل دليل لفظي كوجود " أم " في البيت الأول بخلاف ما بعده.

SAMIN-DURR:6:76#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#3/r4.claim: الأفول means setting, disappearance, or going away; the cited line by Dhū al-Rummah uses الآفلات for setting stars.
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#3/r4.anchor: والأفول: الغيبة والذهاب، يقال: أفل يأفل أفولا، قال ذو الرمة:

SAMIN-DURR:6:76#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#3/r5.claim: الإفال means young sheep, while الأفيل means an undersized foal.
SAMIN-DURR:6:76#3/r5.anchor: والإفال: صغار الغنم، والأفيل: الفصيل الضئيل.

TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r1.claim: The night covered Abraham; Arabic accepts several constructions with janna/ajnā, with the forms using the alif more eloquent in the stated pairings.
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r1.anchor: يقال منه: جن عليه الليل، وجنه الليل، وأجنه، وأجن عليه، وإذا ألقيت (على) كان الكلام بالألف أفصح منه بغير الألف

TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r2.claim: The verb forms are dialectally distributed: jannah al-layl is used by Asad, while ajannah and jannah are used by Tamīm.
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r2.anchor: وجنه الليل في أسد، وأجنه وجنه في تميم

TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r3.claim: The root means to be concealed from sight; the jinn are so named because they are hidden from human eyes, and Arabs apply the root to anything concealed.
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r3.anchor: والجن من ذلك، لأنهم استجنوا عن أعين بني آدم فلا يرون، وكل ما توارى عن أبصار الناس فإن العرب تقول فيه: قد جن

TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r4.speaker: الهذلي
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r4.claim: A Huthalī poem applies janna to water hidden by the dark night, illustrating the sense of concealment.
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r4.anchor: وماء وردت قبيل الكرى … وقد جنه السدف الأدهم

TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r5.speaker: عبيد
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r5.claim: ʿUbayd’s line likewise uses the word for night covering a desolate place.
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r5.anchor: وخرق تصيح البوم فيه مع الصدى … مخوف إذا ما جنه الليل مرهوب

TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r6.claim: The same root describes burying a dead person, as one is covered in the grave.
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r6.anchor: ومنه: أجننت الميت: إذا واريته في اللحد، وجننته.

TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r7.claim: A shield is called a mijann because it covers the person sheltered beneath it.
TAB-FULL:v9p354#2/r7.anchor: ومنه قيل للترس: مجن، لأنه يجن من استجن به فيغطيه ويواريه.

TAB-FULL:v9p356/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p356/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v9p356/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the kingdom shown to Abraham as the sun, moon, and stars, and reports that Abraham worshipped each celestial body until it set before declaring disavowal of what his people associated with God.
TAB-FULL:v9p356/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وكذلك نري إبراهيم ملكوت السموات والأرض وليكون من الموقنين} : يعني به: الشمس والقمر والنجوم

TAB-FULL:v9p356/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p356/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v9p356/r2.claim: Qatādah says the star’s setting taught Abraham that his Lord is everlasting and does not disappear; at the sun he saw a creation greater and brighter than the first two.
TAB-FULL:v9p356/r2.anchor: عن قتادة: {فلما جن عليه الليل رأى كوكبا قال هذا ربي فلما أفل قال لا أحب الآفلين} [الأنعام: 76] : علم أن ربه دائم لا يزول

TAB-FULL:v9p361#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p361#2/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v9p361#2/r1.claim: Ibn Isḥāq glosses afūl as going away and gives the verb forms for a star disappearing or setting.
TAB-FULL:v9p361#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: الأفول: الذهاب، يقال منه: أفل النجم يأفل ويأفل أفولا وأفلا: إذا غاب

TAB-FULL:v9p361#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p361#2/r2.speaker: ذو الرمة
TAB-FULL:v9p361#2/r2.claim: Dhū al-Rummah’s line uses āfilāt for setting stars, illustrating disappearance.
TAB-FULL:v9p361#2/r2.anchor: ومنه قول ذي الرمة: [البحر الطويل] مصابيح ليست باللواتي يقودها … نجوم ولا بالآفلات الدوالك

TAB-FULL:v9p361#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p361#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p361#2/r3.claim: The idiom “where did you disappear from us?” uses afalat to mean that someone went away or was absent.
TAB-FULL:v9p361#2/r3.anchor: ويقال: أين أفلت عنا؟ بمعنى: أين غبت عنا؟

TABATABAI:6:76-78/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:76-78/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:76-78/r1.claim: After debating his father and people about idols, Abraham turns to their astral objects, successively saying “this is my lord” of the star, moon, and sun, with the sun “greater.”
TABATABAI:6:76-78/r1.anchor: ثم إنه عليه السلام بعد الفراغ مما حاج به أباه آزر وقومه في أمر الأصنام يشتغل بأربابها وهي الكوكب والقمر والشمس

TABATABAI:6:76-78/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:76-78/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:76-78/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī reads the demonstratives as words of someone unfamiliar with the star, moon, and sun, who knows only that people worship and sacrifice to them.
TABATABAI:6:76-78/r2.anchor: وهذه التعبيرات أيضا تعبير من كأنه لم ير كوكبا ولا قمرا ولا شمسا

TABATABAI:6:79/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:79/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:79/r2.claim: Abraham lived apart from his father's society, joined him, questioned and refuted idol worship, challenged his people, then successively tested the star, moon, and sun before returning to pure monotheism.
TABATABAI:6:79/r2.anchor: إنما عاش قبل ذلك في معزل من الجو الذي كان يعيش فيه أبوه وقومه ولم يكن يعرف ما يعرفه معاشر المجتمعين من تفاصيل شؤون أجزاء الكون

TABATABAI:6:79/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:79/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:79/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī thinks the sequence likely unfolded over about two days and one night.
TABATABAI:6:79/r3.anchor: وكأنه تم له ذلك في يومين وليلة بينهما تقريبا على ما سنبين إن شاء الله تعالى

ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r7.claim: The night covering someone means it darkened enough to hide him; anything covered may be described with جن or أجن, and both جن عليه الليل and أجنه الليل are used.
ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r7.anchor:
يقال جن عليه الليل وأجنه الليل إذا أظلم حتى يستتر بظلمته ويقال لكل
ما ستر قد جن، وقد أجن

ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r8.claim: Among the expressions for nightfall, the author prefers جن عليه الليل and أجنه الليل.
ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r8.anchor: ولكن الاختيار جن عليه الليل وأجنه الليل

ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r9.claim: Abraham's people worshipped idols, the sun, moon, and stars; once mature enough for reflection and accountability, he examined what they worshipped.
ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r9.anchor:
وقيل إن قوم إبراهيم كانوا يعبدون الأصنام والشمس والقمر
والكواكب، فلما بلغ إبراهيم المبلغ الذي يجب معه النظر

ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r10.claim: Abraham's “this is my lord” repeats his people's claim, as in God's address asking where the partners they claimed were.
ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r10.anchor: قال لهم هذا ربي أي فى زعمكم، كما قال الله

ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r11.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r11.claim: Afala means that the star disappeared.
ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r11.anchor:
فلما أفل).
أي فلما غاب، يقال أفل النجم يأفل وبأفل أفولا، إذا غاب

ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r12.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r12.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r12.claim: Abraham rejects as gods things that rise, travel, and move between places, since that state marks them as created and is shared with things everyone agrees are not gods.
ZAJJAJ:v2p265/r12.anchor:
لا أحب من كانت حالته أن يطلع ويسير على هيئة يتبين معها أنه
محدث منتقل من مكان إلى مكان

TABRISI:6:76-79/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:76-79/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو وورش
TABRISI:6:76-79/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Warsh through al-Bukhārī's route read raʾā kawkaban with fatḥa on rāʾ and kasra on hamza wherever it occurs.
TABRISI:6:76-79/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وورش من طريق البخاري رأى كوكبا بفتح الراء وكسر الهمزة حيث كان

TABRISI:6:76-79/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:76-79/r2.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وخلف ويحيى عن أبي بكر
TABRISI:6:76-79/r2.claim: These readers pronounce both rāʾ and hamza with kasra in raʾā.
TABRISI:6:76-79/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وخلف ويحيى عن أبي بكر رأى بكسر الراء والهمزة

TABRISI:6:76-79/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:76-79/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:76-79/r3.claim: The remaining readers use fatḥa on both letters; Abū ʿAlī's detailed argument for the readings was omitted to avoid length.
TABRISI:6:76-79/r3.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بفتح الراء والهمزة. الحجة: ذكر أبو علي الوجه

TABRISI:6:76-79/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:76-79/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:76-79/r4.claim: Janna, janna-hu, and ajanna describe night darkening until it conceals things; the root also explains why jinn are named for being hidden from sight.
TABRISI:6:76-79/r4.anchor: جن عليه الليل وجنه الليل وأجنه الليل إذا أظلم حتى يستر بظلمته

TABRISI:6:76-79/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:76-79/r5.speaker: الهذلي
TABRISI:6:76-79/r5.claim: The Hudhalī poet uses jannah for water covered by the dark shade before dawn.
TABRISI:6:76-79/r5.anchor: وماء وردت قبيل الكرى وقد جنه السدف الأدهم

TABRISI:6:76-79/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:76-79/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:76-79/r6.claim: Ajanantu and jannantu mean that one buried a dead person in a grave.
TABRISI:6:76-79/r6.anchor: ويقال أجننت الميت وجننته إذا واريته في اللحد

TABRISI:6:76-79/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:76-79/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:76-79/r7.claim: Afala means to set or disappear.

TABRISI:6:76-79/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:76-79/r8.speaker: ذو الرمة
TABRISI:6:76-79/r8.claim: Dhū al-Rumma's poem uses the word āfilāt for setting stars.
TABRISI:6:76-79/r8.anchor:
قال ذو الرمة:
مصابيح ليست باللواتي يقودها نجوم ولا بالآفلات

TABRISI:6:76-79#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:76-79#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:76-79#2/r9.claim: The star Abraham saw is variously identified as Venus or Jupiter.
